arxiv-2603-00799: Ghanem proves energy bounds for a tensor system of coupled nonlinear waves, suited to the structure of Einstein-Yang-Mills in the Lorenz gauge. She bounds the L2 norm of each frame part on its own, splitting off higher order bounds for certain parts. This uses the tensor structure of the waves, a background metric shifting flat space-time, and the bracket term. The split bounds are new and lead to a proof of outer stability of flat space-time.
arxiv-2603-00899: Abiad and four colleagues define a strong nullity parameter for graphs with a marked root vertex. It pairs the nullity of a symmetric matrix with that of the matrix left after deleting the root's row and column. They show the parameter respects graph minors and prove a bifurcation lemma for its interlacing property. With these tools they characterize rooted graphs at each level from zero to five by their minimal minors, tying the families to the older unrooted parameter.
arxiv-2603-01199: Hendrickson and Haefner identify the invariant behind valley-peak modulation, a read-noise metric for ultra-low-noise CMOS sensors. Phase mapping quotients the sensor model by the electron lattice, giving a wrapped-Gaussian density set by read noise alone. It admits lattice-sum and Jacobi theta-function forms. The invariant theta ratio unifies existing approximations as low-order truncations, and a moment method estimates conversion gain and read noise jointly from raw gray values without assuming an electron-number law.
arxiv-2603-01299: Villamil and Gandica analyze a decade of Wikipedia editing, from 2001 to 2010, across eleven language editions to read cultural dynamics through editing rhythms. They cluster each edition by thematic composition and by weekly activity cycle within each theme, testing two normalizations of the temporal view. Linguistic communities show distinct daily and weekly rhythms: Russian and Chinese group together under both views and both metrics, while German and French emerge only from temporal rhythms. Time thus reveals structure that theme alone misses, a neglected dimension in cross-cultural studies of digital traces.
arxiv-2603-01399: Huang and Wen offer Quasar, a training-free plan using low-bit quantizing for the checking stage of speculative drafting, overcoming the memory wall limiting speedup. Speculative drafting splits token making into rapid drafting and side-by-side checking. Checking needs one complete run through the target model and stays memory-flow bound. Hard shape pruning hurts checking truth badly, while quantizing-based checking keeps the logit spread with high faith while cutting memory traffic in half.
arxiv-2603-01599:
Shrinking neural networks to tiny number formats saves memory and power on small devices, but quality often drops. Ningfeng Yang and Tor Aamodt present a format that keeps both speed and information in this 2026 work. Past best formats were either fast to compute with or rich in information, but not both at once.

Their method, BBQ, rests on a simple insight: learning does not care which domain its numbers live in. So the method quantizes with full information care in the input domain, then maps results to a fast domain. Scores beat prior best pre-training methods at four, three, two, and even one bit per weight. The gain grows as the bit width shrinks, which is where edge devices need help most. Code is public for others to test.
arxiv-2603-01799:
Cas Proost and Pieter Bonte reason over streaming facts without starting over at each step in this 2026 work. Data now arrives as fast streams, and stream reasoning seeks live insights from logic rules over that flow. Streams are noisy and volatile, so facts can clash inside any short window of data.

The pair propose new semantics for incremental reasoning over sliding windows of logic facts. Each window materialization, the full set of derived facts, builds on the prior window result. That reuse tackles both stream speed and the real-time demand at once. For clashes, preferred repair semantics pick which facts to keep in a principled way. Semi-naive algorithms then maintain the materialization step by step for a common logic profile, with and without clashes present.
arxiv-2603-01899:
Saikhom Pravash, Thiem Hoang, Archana Soam, and colleagues read magnetic fields in a dark star-forming filament from polarized dust light. Their 2026 work studies a massive, quiet infrared dark cloud with telescope dust polarization data. Aligned non-spherical dust grains polarize their glow, which traces field shape and grain behavior at once.

Denser zones show a polarization hole, where the polarized share drops as brightness and density rise. Field tangling proves too weak to explain that drop in their analysis. Loss of grain alignment efficiency in dense gas fits better, in line with radiative torque theory. That theory says starlight torques spin grains into alignment with the field. Outer zones need a magnetically boosted version of the theory to match their high polarization. Detailed modeling with best-fit grain sizes reproduces the data well.
arxiv-2603-02299:
L Chacón, G Chen, and L Ricketson dispute a plasma simulation claim in this 2026 comment paper. The target study tested a fully implicit particle method that conserves charge and energy. It asked how particle counts per cell affect solution quality. Its authors concluded that more particles per cell are needed once cells exceed a key length.

Chacón and colleagues re-examine one core test, an ion acoustic shock wave. They report procedural flaws in how the original study measured its results. Fixing those flaws, they argue, changes the study's outcome dramatically. On their analysis, the original conclusion does not survive independent scrutiny. The comment is narrow by design: it tests one case in depth rather than every variant in the original work.
arxiv-2603-02499:
Akila Pemasiri, Ethan Goan, Glen Lichtwark, and colleagues estimate gait from video without markers in this 2026 paper. Clinics measure walking with marker-based motion capture, which is costly and slow to set up. Pose estimation from video is cheaper but often too crude for biomechanics. Their framework rebuilds the body in 3D from ordinary video.

From that rebuild, it extracts markers with real biomechanical meaning. Those markers feed OpenSim, a standard tool for joint motion estimation. Timing and joint parameters were checked against marker-based reference data. Agreement was strong, and far better than pose estimation alone. The method stays interpretable, since its markers mirror clinical practice. Scalable, markerless gait checks could reach clinics and field settings alike.
arxiv-2603-02599:
Sunghyeon Woo, Ahreum Seo, Jaegwang Lee, and colleagues share decoding across language models in this 2026 paper. Serving many models at once splits GPU resources by model, wasting capacity. Decoding is memory-bound and cannot batch across models in standard setups. Skewed workloads leave some GPUs idle while others queue.

Their system, SUN, splits a transformer into a prefill part and a decode part. Only the task-specific prefill part is fine-tuned for each model. A single frozen decode part then serves every model in the pool. Routing balances decode requests across shared workers to maximize utilization. Accuracy matched full fine-tuning across tasks and model families. Throughput per GPU doubled in the best case, and a quantized variant ran faster still.
arxiv-2603-02899:
Fabian Kabus, Maren Hackenberg, Julia Hindel, and colleagues blend neural networks with classic statistics to read brain cell movies. Their 2026 paper works with two-photon calcium imaging, where glowing cells reveal activity over time. Neural nets find rich patterns but cannot say which factors drive the motion, while sparse regression can.

Their design embeds a sparse vector autoregressive model inside a convolutional autoencoder that first shrinks the images. A skip connection routes steady spatial detail around the sparse part, so only true time structure enters the readable model. Contribution maps then show which regions drive the learned dynamics. The setup also supports tests comparing time sequences from the same cell unit.
arxiv-2603-03099:
Ruinan Jin, Yingbin Liang, and Shaofeng Zou give the first proof that Adam's edge over plain stochastic gradient descent is real, in a precise sense. Adam converges faster in practice on many problems, yet theory long rated the two methods about equal. Their 2026 analysis isolates Adam's second-moment normalization, the rescaling that steadies each coordinate's step.

Using a stopping-time and martingale argument under the standard bounded-variance assumption, they separate the methods' high-probability guarantees. Adam's dependence on the confidence level is provably gentler, scaling with its square root where SGD must pay the full amount. That sharper tail behavior is a concrete, measurable advantage, not just a heuristic impression. The result helps explain a decade of empirical preference for Adam.
arxiv-2603-03699:
Sirui Yu, Hong Mao, Jinshuang Jin, and Chui-Ping Yang switch on electron teleportation between quantum dots by turning up a force usually treated as a nuisance. Two dots are linked by a pair of Majorana zero modes, the topological quasiparticles, with almost no direct coupling between the modes. Without interactions, two tunneling channels cancel each other out and teleportation between the dots is shut down. Their 2026 paper asks what Coulomb repulsion does.

Using an exact numeric method for the equations of motion with dissipation, the team computes brief currents and current cross-correlation noise. A finite Coulomb interaction lifts the channel degeneracy, and strong nonlocal correlations and inter-dot teleportation switch on. The noise spectrum carries a robust signature, stronger than the signal a small Majorana coupling would give. The strength of that force becomes a practical lab knob for creating and detecting Majorana-mediated transport.
arxiv-2603-04199: Bell and others present Bayesian adversarial privacy. Theoretical and applied privacy research spans an incredibly broad range of methods, emphases, and aims. The paper presents a new quantitative notion of privacy, both contextual and given. Building on data disclosure control and differential privacy ideas, it models disclosure-choice implications in an hostile setting. The definition relies on standard Bayesian choice theory concepts while departing from them in several key respects. Illuminating toy cases highlight the method's specificities.
arxiv-2603-04299: Henestrosa and colleagues test how language models answer users showing Dark Triad traits. The traits studied are Machiavellianism, narcissism, and psychopathy, expressed in prompts of varying severity. Agreeable replies risk reinforcing harmful tendencies, so safer systems must handle escalation from benign to harmful requests. All models lean toward corrective replies, the team finds, though some also give reinforcing or ambivalent output. Behaviour also shifts with severity level and with response sentiment. Safer replies should calm, not feed, harmful talk.
arxiv-2603-04899: Ganggui Ding and team offer FC-VFI, a video frame interpolation method for high-frame-rate slow motion that keeps detail from the start and end frames rather than leaning on generative priors. A plan that builds models over time on latent chains carries true-to-life cues from both endpoints, and semantic matching lines guide structure-aware motion. A loss that punishes time gaps curbs inconsistencies. The system supports 4x and 8x filling in, lifting 30 FPS footage to 120 and 240 FPS at 2560x1440 detail.
arxiv-2603-05399: Sunishchal Dev and team present the Judge Reliability Harness. LLM-based scoring is widely deployed, yet reliability tooling lags. Given a benchmark data set and judge setup, the harness tests binary and ordinal grading. Four judges across four benchmarks covering safety, persuasion, misuse, and agentic actions vary across models and perturbations, highlighting toughness improvement opportunities. No judge is uniformly sound across benchmarks. Tests reveal sameness issues in judging task completion, due to formatting, paraphrasing, verbosity, and flipped labels.
arxiv-2603-05599: Byrne and team fit ovals to scattered-light images of protoplanetary disks to extract dust-scattered surface heights. Their pulling and oval fitting method locates shapes via edge spotting and Gaussian fitting. Oval fitting reveals offsets between oval centers and stellar spots, read as vertical height if rings are circles. The method yields height readings for 92 disks, matching flared shapes, but no single power-law link fits the full sample. Big disks with outer radii above about 150 au show a clear flaring trend.
arxiv-2603-05699: Bentley and team show machine learning can improve growth control and re-doability in pulsed laser laying of oxides. Making LaVO3 films stays hard, because laying is highly off-balance and defects and rival phases pile up. Using Gaussian process Bayesian tuning with lattice traits plus dirt phase information, they map the growth space fast. Tuning weights, the model finds a best region where phase-pure films show minimal sub-band gap soaking. The trained model reveals defect works rivalry tied to excess and surface movement, showing deep growth works.
arxiv-2603-05899: Tong and team propose three bias cutting methods for concept neck image sorting. Concept neck models map images to clear concepts before a sparse one-layer sorter predicts, in theory aiding fairness by masking private proxies like facial traits. Yet concepts leak other information, and early results show only marginal gender bias cuts on data sets like ImSitu. The methods are a top-k concept filter cutting leakage, biased concept removal, and rival de-bias. Results beat prior work on fairness-performance tradeoffs, a big step toward fair, clear sorting.
arxiv-2603-06099: Kishore, Gupta, and Wiita examine optical light curves of the blazar S5 0716+714 from TESS sectors 40, 47, and 53 over about 75 days. The source varied in every sector, and bending power laws beat simple power laws for all but one segment's power spectral density shape. Weighted wavelet Z transform and Lomb-Scargle periodogram searches identify one possible quasi-periodic oscillation in part of sector 40, with a period near 6.5 h and about 95% global significance. Continuous autoregressive moving average modelling shows processes more complex than the simplest damped random walk.
arxiv-2603-06399: Pal and his team set out DiffInf, a diffusion method guided by self influence that mitigates label inconsistencies. Facial attribute classification relies on labeled datasets where traits like age are unclear yet sorted into labels. A sorter is trained and self scores found to identify harmful instances. Instead of dropping influential samples, correction via a diffusion autoencoder aligns content with assigned labels while keeping identity. Edited samples take the place of the old ones, yielding a refined dataset. Across facial attribute work, DiffInf improves reach over noisy label training.
arxiv-2603-06699: Mohammadreza Haghighat and colleagues tackle visual grounding in farm photos, where a phrase must point to one crop or weed plant. They build gRef-CW, the first farm test set for this task, with hard cases where plants look alike, vary in size, or the named plant is absent. Top models show a wide gap on it. Their Weed-VG system scores multi-label relevance in a hierarchy and refines boxes by interpolation.
arxiv-2603-06799: Basu and colleagues prove the existence of a partial system whose Ramsey number grows as a tower of height one less than the uniformity. A partial system here means a uniform hypergraph where every set of a given size sits in at most one edge. Their construction uses the case where that set size is one below the edge size, with at least four colors. The tower growth shows how Ramsey numbers for such sparse hypergraphs can climb extremely fast with uniformity, even under the at-most-one-edge restriction.
arxiv-2603-06899: Cherry and colleagues cut extra PDE solves from Gauss-Newton work for large inverse problems. Each goal or gradient check in PDE-limited optimization usually needs PDE solves, making these problems expensive. Gauss-Newton suits large PDE problems, but full-waveform inversion stalls on extra solves for Jacobian-vector products. Their method needs no solves beyond those for gradients. Full-waveform tests show it matches gradient-method speed while keeping fast settling.
arxiv-2603-07299: Karjol, Shubham and Prathosh find continuous symmetries from spectral fingerprints instead of searching over generator sets. Their key point is that invariance to a subgroup leaves a sparse pattern in how a function spreads across irreducible representations. On maximal tori the method reduces to ordinary multi-dimensional Fourier analysis. Tests from the double pendulum to top-quark tagging show the sparse pattern exposes one-parameter symmetries time and again.
arxiv-2603-07499: Romano and colleagues design an observer that gauges a car's sideslip angle and tire forces from standard sensors alone. Their design joins a single-track linear model with a distributed tire model in terms of hyperbolic partial differential equations. Dynamical inversion then rebuilds lumped and spread states using only yaw rate and lateral acceleration. Tests show it works even under noise and model uncertainty.
arxiv-2603-07899: Debnath and colleagues want power-grid load forecasts with uncertainty estimates that hold up in extreme weather, where standard deep models turn overconfident and fail. Their Bayesian Transformer adds three uncertainty tools to a PatchTST backbone: Monte Carlo Dropout, variational layers with log-uniform weight priors, and stochastic attention with learnable Gaussian noise. A multi-quantile pinball-loss head and isotonic calibration produce sharp intervals with near-nominal coverage. On five grid datasets it led the field, holding coverage near 90 percent through heat waves and cold snaps.
arxiv-2603-08399: Lee and colleagues offer a recipe for stable offline multi-agent reinforcement learning. Despite single-agent offline reinforcement learning achievements, multi-agent learning has struggled to adopt the paradigm, persisting with on-policy training and self-play. One reason is instability in non-linear value decomposition, which led prior works to avoid complex mixing networks for linear decomposition with value regularization from single-agent setups. The authors analyze instability in non-linear value decomposition, proposing scale-invariant normalization. It stabilizes actor-critic training without altering the Bellman fixed point.
arxiv-2603-08599: Fatih Dogangun and colleagues plan robot moves on two levels, with learned symbols on top and checked motion below. Past symbol learners used fixed rules, skipped plan checks, and missed fine motion detail. Their bilevel frame lets probable symbol rules sketch fast plans while learned motion models test them. It beats symbol-only rivals, matches full forward search, and settles most tasks by fast symbol reasoning.
arxiv-2603-08899: Zongyue Qin and colleagues help draft models look ahead in speculative decoding. Drafts that see only the current prefix drift from the target over steps as errors pile up. Their ConFu frame adds contemplate tokens and soft prompts for future signals, a dynamic token mechanism with mixture-of-experts, and anchor-token training, beating EAGLE-3 on acceptance and speed.
arxiv-2603-09199: Geng Chen, Faris A. El-Katri, and Yanbo Hu study fast expanding waves in a gas flow that spreads out from a center point. They track two slope-based quantities, one for waves that thin the gas and one for waves that squeeze it. Using the equations these quantities obey, they mark safe ranges and bound the flow in advance under stated starting assumptions. When both start at or above zero the flow stays smooth; one very low value means a blow-up in finite time.
arxiv-2603-09599: Andreas Rausch and colleagues present a project-based AI Engineering curriculum preparing students for AI-driven agile software development. Many programs still teach agile methods and AI skills separately, mostly by lecture. Their design weaves both through the whole program, with second-semester bachelor teams running seven two-week sprints on a realistic product. AI tools support daily tasks from requirements and backlog work to documentation, testing, and coding, paired with reflection on quality and human responsibility. Early mixed-methods evidence points to hands-on competence growth.
arxiv-2603-09899: Giacomo Borin and coauthors write a guide to using level structures to widen the SQIsign signature scheme. In their general frame, a signer must show an isogeny between public key and commitment that also maps one chosen level structure to another. They work the frame out with isogenies in one and two dimensions. Along the way they give an explicit Deuring correspondence for supersingular curves with level structure.
arxiv-2603-09999: Immordino, Vaiuso and Righi design a help tool based on retrieval for drone safety checks and rule compliance. Applying set safety frames such as Specific Operations Risk Assessment takes more and more effort as drone use grows. Their tool draws only on trusted rule texts, cites the bits behind each answer, and stays cautious when proof is thin. It backs expert judgement only, never taking its place and never deciding on its own, so checks stay traceable.
arxiv-2603-10199: Gao and coauthors speed up Policy Dual Averaging for learning in action spaces that run on a scale with no steps. That method takes value function fits well, yet each choice needs an optimisation sub problem that is costly to solve. Their actor version learns a policy net that stands in for those solutions, cutting run time while keeping firm guarantees. Tests quantify how actor error shifts convergence, and robotics and control tasks beat PPO.
arxiv-2603-10399: Roy A Lacey examines a recent scaling analysis of net-proton cumulants that was read as evidence for a critical end point in the QCD phase diagram. His note questions several steps in that construction. Treating an acceptance window as the physical system size is one concern, along with acceptance-driven effects on the susceptibility and the handling of scaling fields. Taken together, he argues, the reported scaling does not uniquely establish critical dynamics, nor a critical end point near the claimed baryon chemical potential.
arxiv-2603-10499: Orest Pavlosiuk and co-authors report that the half-Heusler material DyPtBi breaks a usual trade-off, showing large transverse and longitudinal magnetothermopower at once. In well-compensated semimetals the longitudinal part is normally held down by near-perfect electron-hole balance. Here thermal excitation in a zero-gap material drives an ambipolar effect, and imperfect compensation leaves an asymmetry between carriers, so both parts grow large. Values stayed strong even at room temperature in a weak field, and a DyPdBi comparison shows how much band structure matters.
arxiv-2603-10599: Ivan Bioli and Mikel Mendibe Abarrategi document a JAX package for quasi-Newton methods in the self-scaled Broyden family, built on Optimistix. It covers BFGS, DFP, and Broyden methods with their self-scaled variants, plus L-BFGS, and adds a zoom line search meeting the strong Wolfe conditions. The authors bill it as a short technical note rather than a research paper: no new method is claimed. Its aim is to ease adoption of these optimizers in the JAX community, with installs via PyPI.
arxiv-2603-10999: Milos Ciganovic, Federico D'Amario, and Massimiliano Tancioni adapt double machine learning to macroeconomic time series. Double machine learning is a causal estimation method. Its usual cross-fitting wastes the structure of such data. Their reverse cross-fitting step exploits the time-reversibility of stationary series. This uses samples better. They prove the conditions under which the estimator stays asymptotically valid. A calibration rule targets a Goldilocks zone of tuning choices. An application to local projections estimates a dynamic effect. It estimates the effects of a rise in Tier 1 regulatory capital.
arxiv-2603-11099: Zeyuan Guo and coauthors tokenize graphs so that plain pretrained transformers can read them. They borrow the byte pair encoding that powers large language model tokenizers. Their reversible serialization turns a graph into a sequence. It loses no information. Global substructure statistics guide the process, so frequent patterns surface often. Those patterns merge into meaningful tokens. Unmodified BERT-style transformers then reach state-of-the-art results on fourteen graph benchmarks. They often beat both graph neural networks and specialized graph transformers.
arxiv-2603-11199: Eike Cramer and coauthors speed up Bayesian optimization for partially known systems by fusing its learned model with known physics equations. Standard Bayesian optimization learns a direct input-to-objective map and can need prohibitively many expensive trials, especially in high-dimensional nonlinear problems. Their hybrid writes out the known mechanistic equations and infers the missing pieces with a Gaussian process, entering the process as a constraint. On an in-silico distillation optimization it beats the standard loop clearly and sometimes converges in a single iteration.
arxiv-2603-11299: Yibai Li and coauthors argue that artificial intelligence and blockchain pull against each other. One moves toward central power, the other away from it. They say the tension is productive rather than fatal. The editorial frames the two as a matched pair. AI concentrates power through data and resource monopolies. Blockchain counters with decentralization and security. It offers decentralized data management, computation, and governance. In return, AI can automate smart contracts, curation, and threat detection. The authors call for a new field, decentralized intelligence.
arxiv-2603-11399: Dat Tran and coauthors build a shopping assistant for users who do not yet know what they want, using entropy as the single signal that steers questions and rankings alike. Ambiguous early queries once forced a bad choice between endless clarifying questions and overconfident recommendations that collapse the search too soon. Their system filters a candidate product set dynamically and asks the follow-up question with the highest expected information gain. Leftover uncertainty feeds diversification instead of forced resolution, yielding fewer wasted questions and more informative, diverse sets.
arxiv-2603-11499: Meguro, Ishizuka, and Nomura study spin-motive force past the linear response regime, beyond the Thouless-pump picture. Spin-motive force is the electric current that magnetization dynamics induce in a material. In linear response, that current is purely AC. At nonlinear order, the team shows, it gains both a DC part and a second-harmonic part. Both parts trace back to quantum geometry in a mixed space of momentum and magnetization. A Luttinger model check finds a measurable signal even in the insulating regime.
arxiv-2603-11699: Gil and co-authors merge single-stage stellarator design with stochastic coil optimization to harden the device against coil errors. The plasma boundary, from an MHD solver in fixed-boundary mode, links to randomly perturbed coils through the squared flux. That setup steers the search away from sharp local minima toward sturdier shapes. Two new designs come out: one quasi-axisymmetric and one quasi-helically symmetric. Under later coil perturbations, they beat standard methods on squared flux, quasisymmetry, and particle loss.
arxiv-2603-11799: Brännvall shows that three membership inference attacks, LiRA, RMIA, and BASE, are one method in disguise. All three fit a single exponential-family log-likelihood ratio framework, differing in assumptions and in how many parameters each point gets. The view yields a BASE1-4 ladder from RMIA to LiRA, and a rule: match attack complexity to the shadow-model budget. He then proposes BaVarIA, a Bayesian variance attack that steadies variance estimates at small budgets. Across 12 testbeds and 7 budgets, BaVarIA matches or beats LiRA on average.
arxiv-2603-12199: Chu derives Hawking radiation as tunneling inside a quantum picture of black holes. An earlier proposal casts a quantum black hole as a fuzzy sphere with a half-filled Fermi sea. Decay then means tunneling toward a smaller fuzzy sphere. Fermion number conservation seems to block the move, since the sea shrinks as the sphere falls. A monopole on the fuzzy sphere supplies zero modes that soak up the excess states. The rate matches Page's semi-classical result, and unitarity stays manifest.
arxiv-2603-12399: Özcan, Orguner, and Oguz plan pushing and press-and-slide moves with mode-aware reduced-order models. Planar contact tasks mix hybrid mechanics, under-actuation, and asymmetric friction. Their core move is to abstract wrench-twist limit surfaces into a small library of intuitive models. Single-arm and bimanual contact topologies map to simple forms, like a unicycle for press-and-slide. Trajectory generation anchors to those models, then an algebraic allocator splits feasible contact forces. Simulations across one- and two-arm tasks run fast with no optimization loop.
arxiv-2603-12499: Rathjens, Schiewer, Wiskott, and Subramoney probe how Mamba handles sequence lengths beyond its training range. Mamba draws wide interest as a fast sequence model that rivals transformers at low cost. Yet its scores can drop when test sequences run longer than training ones. The team uses a controlled vision task where Mamba rebuilds images from patch sequences. Stage-by-stage checks show Mamba adapts its strategy to the lengths it saw in training. Those strategies then fail outside that range. A length-adaptive variant improves scores across training lengths.
arxiv-2603-13099: Wayner Barrios and SouYoung Jin introduce CRYSTAL, a benchmark that grades multimodal reasoning by its steps, not just final answers. Its 6,372 cases carry verifiable intermediate steps for scoring. Two metrics check step precision and recall, with a penalty for steps out of order. Four models drafted the reference chains, which were clustered and passed through human gates. Tests of 20 models exposed cherry-picking and jumbled chains that answer scores hide. A causal process reward then lifted step scores by 32% in training.
arxiv-2603-13199: Daniel Goodair studies a vanishing viscosity limit for the 3D stochastic Navier-Stokes equations between two plates. The flow has a Dirichlet no-slip condition at the plates. Its viscosity splits into horizontal and vertical parts that shrink at different rates. Transport-stretching noise, driven by cylindrical Brownian motion, is scaled by each part in turn. Goodair proves that a sequence of weak martingale solutions converges to the strong Euler solution. One hard point is that the anisotropic scaling breaks a key property of the noise.
arxiv-2603-13299: Nirmalendu Prakash and co-authors release DreamReader, a toolkit for studying text-to-image diffusion models. Work on how these models work inside has been split into lone tests with no shared frame. DreamReader joins activation extraction, causal patching, ablations, and steering in one system. It works across model types and time steps, with tests run in set batches. Three new tools let users tune parts of a model and steer it with probe scores. Case studies show LLM-born methods can steer image models in a controlled way.
arxiv-2603-13499: Yanjun Han, Abhishek Shetty, and Jacob Shkrob study mean estimation from heteroskedastic Gaussian observations. Variances are unknown and may vary arbitrarily across observations, which adds many nuisance parameters. Their empirical Bayes approach models the data as a normal scale mixture and computes a profile maximum likelihood estimator for the mean. It achieves near-optimal error bounds across heteroskedastic models in the literature. For the subset-of-signals problem, it adapts to the minimax rate for all signal sizes with no tuning parameters.
arxiv-2603-13599: Michalis Deligiannis, Marco Scarsini, and Xavier Venel study dynamic wholesale pricing under censored-demand learning. In their two-tier supply chain, firms share POS data and learn demand from censored observations. When stockouts occur, unmet demand is unobserved, so order quantity shapes both profit and future signal quality. The manufacturer can speed or slow learning through wholesale prices, while the retailer weighs inventory effects on future information. They prove a Markov perfect equilibrium exists for Weibull demand, and uniqueness for exponential demand. Simulations show public learning creates conflicting incentives.
arxiv-2603-13799: Li and co-authors build DyG-RoLLM, a tool that clusters nodes in graphs that change over time. Unlike black-box methods, it explains why clusters form and how they shift. Node features are split into a role part and a cluster part. Five role types, such as Leader and Connector, act as anchors that a language model can read. A layered reasoning step then gives clusters plus plain-language reasons. Tests on ten benchmarks show strong, robust results.
arxiv-2603-13899: Virovlyansky and co-authors describe a way to calibrate an underwater sound source inside a reflective test tank. The trick uses the odd transparency of the water-air boundary for a shallow source. That boundary blocks wall and bottom echoes from reaching the air above. The field in air then matches a known formula for open water. Measuring sound levels in air thus gives the source strength in water, with no need for a quiet tank.
arxiv-2603-14099: Seydou and Sharma present DeepFix, an agentic tool that tests full machine learning pipelines and suggests fixes. Standard test-case methods often miss deep bugs in modern ML systems and say little about repairs. DeepFix first runs Deepchecks to hunt for faults across the pipeline. An AI agent then writes a ranked bug report with plain explanations and severity scores. Each report also proposes ways to fix the faults found. The tool fits several kinds of ML systems and drops into existing pipelines.
arxiv-2603-14299: Park and co-authors compare how learners ask questions during CPR training with virtual agents in two media. One agent appears in augmented reality in the room, and the other on a screen. Their 5W1H framework sorts questions by who, what, when, where, why, and how. The AR agent drew more and longer questions aimed at clarification, with higher felt presence. The screen agent drew more questions about refining procedure. Presence shaped when and what learners asked, filtered by their learning habits.
arxiv-2603-14599: Silva proves that asymptotic entropy varies continuously on free solvable groups. The entropy is read as a function of the step distribution. The measures in view are non-degenerate and have finite Shannon entropy. The groups are the free solvable groups S_{d,m}. Rank d is at least three, and derived length m is at least two. Continuity means small shifts in the step law yield small shifts in entropy. The result settles how stable this group invariant is under such shifts.
arxiv-2603-15099: Lastovicka gives a new proof that relational algebra is complete for allowed formulas of first-order logic. The proof routes through cylindric algebra, which already embeds relational algebra in a clean way. That detour makes the completeness argument more algebraic than earlier versions. He also derives an algorithm from the proof. The algorithm turns any allowed formula into an equal relational expression. The goal is a proof that can extend to models with incomplete or vague information.
arxiv-2603-15299: Stinis proposes a classifier that runs its input through a chaotic system before deciding. Data vectors are lifted into a higher-dimensional space and used as starting states. A chaotic dynamical system then evolves them for a fixed time span. The evolved state feeds a trainable softmax classifier. On perturbed orthogonal vectors with up to twenty classes, the method trained faster and classified better than plain softmax baselines. He also explains the gain and gives a way to pick the best evolution time.
arxiv-2603-15599: Derehag, Calva, and Ghiurau present SmartSearch, a tool that searches raw chat history for past facts. Many memory systems pay large language models to structure chats at intake. SmartSearch skips that step and uses plain matching rules plus entity search. A learned ranker then fuses two ranking signals on CPU in about 650 milliseconds. The authors report 93.5 percent on LoCoMo and 88.4 percent on LongMemEval-S. It also uses far fewer tokens than full-context baselines.
arxiv-2603-15699: Krupp and co-authors probe whether run time can stand in for energy use. API language models hide their hardware and their power draw. Users see only slow or fast replies. The team compares time-based estimates with real meter readings. Locally hosted twin models supply the ground truth. Timing patterns even reveal which GPU an API model runs on. That clue grounds firmer energy estimates for end users. The work targets a clearer view of hidden inference costs.
arxiv-2603-15799: Gupta and Sreenivasamurthy turn written access rules into runnable Rego code. Hand translation of access prose is slow and error-prone. Their Prose2Policy pipeline handles the full path in modules. Stages detect policies, extract parts, and validate schemas. Linting, compilation, and auto-built tests follow in line. On the ACRE dataset, accepted policies compiled at 95.3 percent. Auto tests passed 82.2 percent of positive cases. Negative cases passed at 98.9 percent. The tool targets Zero Trust and compliance settings.
arxiv-2603-15899: O'Connor and co-authors report a Type Ia supernova inside a merger-made ring. Two near-equal galaxies collided head-on and raised a vast ring. The ring, nicknamed Pika's Halo, spans about 70 kpc around. SN 2025adpq sits on the ring, 11.4 kpc from the main nucleus. Spectra show fresh star formation plus old starlight signs. The team proposes an old progenitor flung out by the collision wave. Broad delay times block a firm ruling, they note. Offset supernovae may often trace such displaced old groups.
arxiv-2603-16199: Sowmya and co-authors predict alpha-decay half-lives for 154 actinide nuclei. The nuclei span atomic numbers 89 to 103. Their tool is the DDM3Y effective interaction, built with a double-folding model. Half-lives come from the WKB approximation. The results track measured values better than four older semi-empirical models. A standard deviation of 1.76 supports the method. The work helps judge the stability of heavy and new isotopes.
arxiv-2603-16299: Kirkham introduces PyPhonPlan, an open Python toolkit for modeling how speech sounds are planned. The toolkit couples dynamic neural fields with task dynamic simulations. Users can define planning, perception, and memory fields. They can also set couplings between fields and gestural inputs. Field activity then drives tract variable trajectories. An example links production and perception through a shared memory field. The package ships with runnable examples for speech research.
arxiv-2603-16599: Rimoldi and co-authors steer city traffic with data-driven perimeter control. Modeling traffic well enough for control design is slow and costly. Learning methods need simulators or choke on sparse data. Their approach rests on behavioral systems theory. Data-enabled predictive control then steers lights across the network. A detailed Zürich simulation tests the method. The run is among the largest closed-loop traffic simulations reported. Scores cover total travel time and CO2 emissions.
arxiv-2603-16799: Müssnich and Vieira extend the tenfold way, the symmetry classification of free fermion systems, to weakly interacting ones. The tenfold way underlies the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors, framed in K-theory. The authors realize the spectra KU and KO through time evolution operators, with explicit suspension maps. They define weakly interacting operators geometrically, as the complement of a cut locus. Their main result is that the weakly interacting spectra retract onto the free ones. So the tenfold way stays stable under weak interactions.
arxiv-2603-16999: Bruno and co-authors study the continuum limit of spin foams, a path integral approach to quantum gravity. Spin foam amplitudes live on spacetime triangulations, so this limit is a central open problem. The authors build an axiomatic framework in the spirit of Atiyah's field theories. Orders on triangulations make the limit precise. They prove a no-go result: strong convergence forces a topological theory. They then weaken convergence to a distributional sense. In that setting, the cylinder amplitude yields a rigging map and a canonical Hilbert space.
arxiv-2603-17099: Oliveira Guimarães and co-authors present a vectorizer for Verilog hardware designs. Vectorization replaces many scalar operations with one vector operation. It is routine in software compilers but rare in Verilog, where tools resolve signals wire by wire anyway. The authors argue the gain is symbolic: verification tools scale better when a bus is one symbolic entity. Their vectorizer builds on the CIRCT infrastructure and handles several assignment patterns. On 1,157 designs, the Jasper tool saw elaboration time and memory use fall sharply.
arxiv-2603-17199: Mirtaheri and Belkin detect motivated reasoning in language models by probing their internal activations. In multiple choice tests with an injected hint, models may shift answers toward the hint and then rationalize the choice without naming the hint. The authors train supervised probes on the model's residual stream. Probes applied before any chain of thought predict motivated reasoning as well as a monitor that reads the full trace. Probes applied after generation do better still.
arxiv-2603-17299: Tao, Tang, and Wei study how the optical variability of turn on changing look galaxies depends on timescale. These galaxies are picked out as their broad emission lines appear or strengthen. Using Zwicky Transient Facility light curves for 106 objects, the team measures variability amplitudes at three rest frame timescales. The strongest trends sit on monthly scales. There, variability falls as optical luminosity and Eddington ratio rise. At longer timescales the links weaken or vanish. Black hole mass shows no robust link on its own.
arxiv-2603-17599: Catoire, Genuer, and Proust-Lima sort out prediction when data go missing. Inference leans on the missing-at-random rule, yet some biased-looking methods predict well under any mechanism. Their framework splits targets by whether the observation flag itself feeds the forecast. That split sorts mechanisms by when the two targets match. Both targets can be predicted under weaker rules than missing-at-random, they prove. A trauma injury case shows the stakes.
arxiv-2603-17999: DuPont and Quataert simulate gas accretion onto equal-mass binaries in a uniform medium. They vary the adiabatic index and the Bondi radius over the binary spacing. Cold, isothermal gas accretes near the full Bondi rate at high compactness. Hotter gas limits itself: orbital shocks make entropy and turbulence that cut the rate sharply. A time-scale test tells which regime a given binary falls into.
arxiv-2603-18099: The ATLAS Collaboration searches for lepton-flavour violating tau decays into three muons. They use proton-proton data at 13 TeV from 2016 to 2018, totaling 137 inverse femtobarns. The search leans on the W to tau channel for trigger gains, plus heavy-flavour sources. A multivariate step splits signal from background before an unbinned fit to the three-muon mass. Data match the background-only view, setting a limit of 8.7 times ten to the minus eight.
arxiv-2603-18399: Wei and co-authors speed up Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency quantum memory with shortcuts to adiabaticity. Fast storage breaks the adiabatic limit and excites a lossy intermediate state. A counter-diabatic auxiliary field shortens writing time while suppressing that transient population. The scheme works across varied control and signal pulse shapes and tolerates drive flaws. It keeps high storage performance even with imperfect single-photon writing and Rydberg blockade.
arxiv-2603-18599: Kang and co-authors speed up image generation with SJD-PAC, a draft-free decoding scheme. Speculative Jacobi decoding drafts tokens without a separate draft model. Complex image regions reject drafts often, which slows output. Proactive drafting raises local acceptance in those hard regions. An adaptive step keeps validating after a first rejection instead of resampling all. The pair of fixes lengthens the average accepted run per step. Tests report a 3.8 times speedup with no loss in image quality.
arxiv-2603-19299: Kuo and co-authors release PRIME-CVD, a fake patient data set built for teaching heart risk modeling. Real health records are locked away by privacy rules, which blocks hands-on training. The set holds 50,000 synthetic adults in primary prevention for heart disease. It is built from a causal graph set by the user and public Australian stats. One asset is clean and ready for analysis tasks. A second reshapes the same cohort into a messy, record-style database. Both support lessons in cleaning, causal logic, and risk work.
arxiv-2603-19399: Parvez and co-authors study how well language models debug contest code, and build a tool to help. Their DePro fixes given code rather than writing fresh solutions from scratch. It builds a brute-force reference, stress tests the code, and refines with model guidance. On 13 faulty Codeforces entries, it reaches correct solutions in every case. Debug tries drop by up to 64 percent against the baselines. Mean time saved is 7.6 minutes per problem versus human debuggers. Zero-shot model debugging also trails the tool.
arxiv-2603-19599: Jin and co-authors present PIACN, a physics-informed network for predicting how information cascades spread online. Prior deep models read early cascades but miss broad macroscopic patterns. They also ignore how content type shapes spread. PIACN models the macro patterns of diffusion with a physics-informed design. An adaptive clustering mechanism accounts for content heterogeneity. Tests on three real data sets beat prior state-of-the-art methods. The work targets high-value delivery and public opinion monitoring.
arxiv-2603-19699: Chu and co-authors study large steady solitary water waves with general vorticity. Such waves may have overhanging profiles, so the surface is not a simple graph. A conformal change of variables moves the problem to a fixed strip. Small waves come first from a centre-manifold argument. A global analytic bifurcation then extends them to large amplitude. The branches cover analytic vorticity functions with no strong limits on the flow. The work goes beyond constant vorticity and flat-profile cases.
arxiv-2603-20199: Hundiwala and Monroy-Hernández test AnchorNote, an augmented reality tool that turns speech into spatial sticky notes. Teams brainstorming together can speak an idea and pin its summary in shared space. Live transcription plus model summarization creates each note on the spot. Twenty participants tried it in a two-phase study with grouping tasks. The tool cut writing effort for the group. It also added coordination costs and changed how people timed and phrased ideas. The authors draw design lessons for future co-located AR collaboration tools.
arxiv-2603-20399: Friederich and Tyagi ask whether quantum field theory can grow out of time-symmetric stochastic mechanics. Their aim is a picture where all observables hold sharp values. That would sidestep the quantum measurement problem entirely. They derive a generalized Liouville equation under natural constraints. The result is a Fokker-Planck equation with a special diffusion matrix. It is symmetric, traceless, and built from the Hamiltonian's Hessian. They then show the Schrödinger equation for some bosonic theories takes exactly this form.
arxiv-2603-20499: Kamgarpour and Whitbread solve the isoclinic Deligne-Simpson problem for exceptional groups. This finishes a program started by earlier researchers. The problem asks when certain local systems with prescribed data exist. Their route uses the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence to change settings. Emptiness questions become point counts on braid varieties over finite fields. Those varieties attach to periodic braids in the problem. As a by-product, they gain new rigid irregular connections. The method echoes Lusztig's map between Weyl group and unipotent classes.
arxiv-2603-20599: Dassi and co-authors build an error estimator for a virtual element method on the buckling eigenvalue problem. The method uses C1 elements on general polytopal meshes. It also adds nonlinear plane stress effects in two and three dimensions. Their estimator is fully computable and sits in the open vem++ library. They prove it is reliable and efficient with standard tools. Tests in 2D and 3D show sharp accuracy and robust behavior.
arxiv-2603-20699: Harada and Yamaguchi study average weight enumerators of double Toeplitz codes. These codes extend the older double circulant family. Weight enumerators count codewords by their number of nonzero entries. The paper works out the average form of these counts. As a use, they probe which minimum weights can occur over small fields. The fields in play have two, three, and four elements. They also classify codes with the largest minimum weights at moderate lengths.
arxiv-2603-20999: Aiersilan and Yang present OrbitStream, a training-free system for adaptive 360 degree video streaming in teleoperation. Two problems meet here: predicting where the operator will look, and adapting bitrate over shaky wireless links. OrbitStream treats gaze prediction as a gravity problem, where semantic objects pull attention. A saturation based controller manages the buffer. On object rich traces, it predicts viewports with high zero-shot accuracy. Across thousands of simulations, it ranks second of twelve methods on quality of experience, with fast decisions.
arxiv-2603-21599: Dipthi and Desikan train a generative model to fake electron neutrino events, a slow step in particle physics. Full Monte Carlo runs cost too much time. Their model is a conditional Wasserstein GAN, guided by the incoming neutrino energy. A gradient penalty keeps training stable. It outputs the full event summary, with no variables dropped. Three channels are covered: inverse beta decay, neutral current, and elastic scattering, from 10 to 31 MeV. Fakes matched held-out GENIE data on spread and on links between variables.
arxiv-2603-21699: Bied and co-authors redesign job recommendation for the French public employment service. Platforms usually rank jobs by clicks or hire chances, not by job seeker welfare. Their model values a vacancy on two axes: how much the worker likes it and how likely an application is to succeed. Welfare-optimal ranking blends both into an expected-surplus index. Two randomized field experiments tested live algorithms against that benchmark. Model-guided rankings beat existing approaches and came close to the welfare optimum, showing large practical gains for seekers.
arxiv-2603-21799: Vokrouhlický sharpens the math of the light-time effect in triple star systems. When a third star orbits an eclipsing binary, the binary's center of mass moves toward and away from us. Eclipse times then arrive early or late, since light speed is finite. Vokrouhlický gives a more exact formula for light travel inside the binary itself. He also adds a term for the coupling between the binary orbit and the third star's motion. The inner correction may be measurable when the period ratio is under about twenty.
arxiv-2603-22099: Brugnoli and co-authors test machine-learned atomic potentials on a water-in-salt electrolyte. Such liquids resist ab initio modeling over long times. The team evaluates several MACE potentials on a 21 molal lithium salt solution. They try foundation models as shipped, fine-tuned versions, and models trained from scratch. Their simulations match measured structure factors closely. Fine-tuning beats training from scratch, above all on hard-to-sample setups like short lithium-lithium distances. They also warn that some dispersion corrections can hurt, depending on the reference functional.
arxiv-2603-22399: Baglio and co-authors design drugs with a style-based quantum generative network. Classic GANs are hard to train and can collapse to a few outputs. Quantum models may dodge those traps with fewer parameters. Their design encodes noise at each rotation gate of the circuit. A gradient penalty in the loss also fights mode collapse. A variational autoencoder first maps molecules into a latent space for the quantum model. They test the setup on simulators and on IBM quantum hardware.
arxiv-2603-22499: Flynt presents OrgForge-IT, a synthetic benchmark for testing language models on insider threat detection. Fake data often contradicts itself, so a fixed simulation engine holds the ground truth while models write only the surface prose. The corpus spans 51 days of records that are more than nine tenths noise. Ten models are ranked on four scenarios built to defeat quick, single-day triage. The results split sharp verdicts from noisy ones and expose weak spots like blaming the wrong victim.
arxiv-2603-22799: Matheny, Nguyen, and Nguyen improve detection of idioms and figurative language. Idioms carry one meaning that is not the sum of their words. Tokenization makes such phrases hard for language models to spot. The authors fine-tune BERT and RoBERTa models with two losses. A slot loss pairs with a span contrastive loss that reweights hard negatives. The models reach state-of-the-art sequence accuracy on existing datasets. Tests support the contrastive loss and its wider use. They also propose a combined score for span awareness and overall performance.
arxiv-2603-23399: Sheng recasts exact density-functional theory as two parallel ensemble hierarchies. One covers interacting systems and grows from Lieb's ensemble form. The other covers noninteracting systems from exact ensemble theory. In optimization terms, N-representability is primal feasibility, and duality equates the primal and dual values. The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem gives a unique local potential when one is attained. The Kohn-Sham scheme couples the two sides on their shared density domain. Fractional particle numbers then yield piecewise linearity and the derivative discontinuity.
arxiv-2603-23499: Min and nine co-authors tackle optical flow in corrupted real-world video. Flow models trained on clean data break down under blur, noise, and compression damage. Their fix borrows features from image restoration diffusion models. Those features sense corruption well but ignore time. The team adds attention across nearby frames, which reveals a knack for matching points. DA-Flow fuses those features with plain convolutional ones in a refining loop. Under heavy damage, it beats current flow methods across several benchmarks by a wide gap.
arxiv-2603-23699: Cosyn and Weiss lay the theory groundwork for electron scattering off a polarized spin-1 target. This first part gives the general cross section and spin measures for such targets. Their math stays fully covariant, built from four-vectors and invariant spin terms. A spin density matrix carries both vector and tensor polarization. They split the cross section by spin and angle into invariant structure functions. Photon helicity amplitudes with known symmetries check the formulas. The results hold across all zones of the final state.
arxiv-2603-23799: Golooba and Woldegerima tackle unstable training in physics-informed neural networks for disease models. These networks mix noisy clinical data with a compartmental model such as SEIR. Their data loss and physics loss often push gradients in opposed directions. That clash can stall learning. Their method, conflict-gated gradient scaling, uses cosine similarity to adjust the penalty weight. It eases the physics term when gradients clash and restores it when they align. They prove a standard convergence rate and report better peak recovery.
arxiv-2603-23899: Anwar and co-authors present SM-Net, a model that generates stellar spectra from three basic parameters. It takes effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity as inputs. Training merges four stellar libraries into one wider, smoother grid. The grid spans temperatures from 2,000 to 190,000 K and a broad wavelength range. SM-Net interpolates smoothly across library boundaries and fills masked flux regions from learned patterns. Test errors stay low across 11,530 spectra, and it makes over 14,000 spectra per second on one GPU.
arxiv-2603-23999: Wang and co-authors demonstrate a faster holonomic quantum gate scheme in a trapped calcium ion. Holonomic gates resist some control errors, but fixed pulse-area rules make small-angle gates slow. Their brachistochrone scheme relaxes that rule, and a composite version adds further gains. They build a pX gate under the classic, brachistochrone, and composite protocols. Tests with dissipation, Rabi errors, and detuning errors show the new schemes beat the classic one. Keeping excited-state population low helps both fidelity and robustness, they find.
arxiv-2603-24199: Csimma presents a repeatable method for building Qt apps with C++ fronts and Agda backends. The agda2hs compiler and Haskell bindings made such apps possible, but no shared methodology existed. Csimma adapts the Model-View-ViewModel pattern to models written in functional languages. A software kit eases installation and automates compilation. He compares ways to use Haskell built-ins inside Agda code. He also gives a new Haskell future design that supports interruption, even through foreign calls. Benchmarks show agda2hs is viable against rival tools.
arxiv-2603-24299: Clark reframes mortality forecasting as motion through a low-dimensional score space. Classic Lee-Carter style methods extrapolate time trends and underpredict life expectancy far ahead. Clark decomposes Human Mortality Database data with a Tucker tensor model. The mortality transition turns out to follow mainly a one-dimensional flow. A speed function moves the level, and trajectory functions give full age and sex schedules. In leave-country-out tests over 50 years, its bias is far smaller than rival methods, with lower error at every age.
arxiv-2603-24499: Abdesselam proves a central limit theorem for the number of connected components in random coverings of a fixed manifold. Such coverings are generated by sampling homomorphisms from the manifold's fundamental group into a symmetric group. The theorem covers the case where that group is nilpotent. It extends an earlier result with Starr for the torus, where the group is free abelian. The proof uses work by du Sautoy and Grunewald on subgroup growth zeta functions, plus Delange's version of the Wiener-Ikehara Tauberian theorem.
arxiv-2603-24599: Wang and co-authors propose a learnable paradigm for stacked intelligent metasurfaces. A SIM stacks programmable metasurface layers that compute directly in the electromagnetic wave domain. Noting the structural similarity between SIMs and neural networks, they design a learnable SIM architecture and a matching learning framework for 6G. Two signal processing schemes follow: one separates multi-user signals, the other splits communication signals from jamming. Tests show better spectrum use and anti-jamming ability in a lightweight design, pointing toward efficient wireless infrastructure.
arxiv-2603-24799: Ünsal investigates beta functions of Yang-Mills theory and adjoint QCD in a self-dual background field. In the deep ultraviolet, the coupling runs with the standard beta function. Treating the background as a superselection sector, the theory abelianises below the scale set by the field and stays abelian in the deep infrared. In between, the coupling still runs even though no charged modes propagate. Only exact zero modes drive that running, so the beta coefficient comes out integer-quantised. Ünsal conjectures an emergent effective theory governs the abelian dynamics.
arxiv-2603-24999: Hardy, Gilbert, and Domingue offer a fast screen for bad test items in large exams and AI benchmarks. Their tool, the signed isotonic R2, asks how much of one item's pattern a monotone curve on another item can explain. It keeps the sign of the link, taken from a rank measure. Adding these pair scores gives each item a grade. Across three AI sets and two human tests, the grade ranked flawed items near the top. The fits take seconds and need no fixed model form.
arxiv-2603-25199: Wen, Wang, and Wang build TacSIm, a dataset and test for copying football tactics, not just chasing wins. Prior work scores goals and win proxies, which says little about team shape. TacSIm uses Premier League broadcast footage. It maps all 22 players' starts and moves onto standard pitch coordinates. A model must replay one team's full behavior in attack or defense. Scoring compares pitch occupancy and movement vectors over set spans. Baselines run in one shared simulator, so style can be judged by numbers and by eye.
arxiv-2603-25599: Hong, Barton, and Neild present a method to track how uncertainty shifts bifurcations in nonlinear systems. Their framework joins continuation methods with parametric sensitivities and extremal conditions. It traces the extreme response points as the uncertainty range grows. Then it follows those points as a control parameter varies. This gives the widest response margins at each step. They test it on a two-degree-of-freedom oscillator. The method reveals an isolated response branch, an isola, that the fixed-parameter system lacks.
arxiv-2603-25699: Sung and co-authors test whether a neural network can take over a classic machine learning pipeline. Their teacher is a random forest, one of the best tools on many tasks. A student network learns to mimic the forest's output. This would allow joint tuning and a single engine for many tasks. They try many network shapes on 100 OpenML tasks. For most tasks, the student matched the teacher when the shape was well chosen. They also test using the forest itself to pick good network settings.
arxiv-2603-25999: Wang and co-authors constrain a quantum cosmology model that treats dark energy as dynamic. In this JCDM model, the trace of the Schouten tensor plays the dark energy role. They fit it with CMB, DESI baryon acoustic, chronometer, and supernova data. For a flat universe, the Hubble constant comes out near 66.95, with matter density 0.3419. A curved fit favors slight positive curvature and a higher Hubble value near 69.13. The model matches late-time data well, they report. It strains to fit early and late data at once.
arxiv-2603-26099: Oh and co-authors study what happens when knowledge workers lose access to language models. They ran a four-day diary study with ten frequent users. Withdrawal exposed gaps in how tasks get done, the team reports. Left to work alone, participants reclaimed professional values they had let slip. Daily habits also showed how deeply model use had become the norm. The authors frame these tools as infrastructure for modern knowledge work. They propose value-driven use as a way to protect professional judgment.
arxiv-2603-26299: Jeong, Lee, and Yoon propose TARA-Merging, a way to merge several LoRA adapters without losing what each one learned. Naive merging can mute key update directions and stress minor ones. Their method views the problem through subspace coverage and directional imbalance. It sets merge weights with a preference-weighted loss while keeping task subspaces intact. Across eight vision tests and six language tests, TARA beats plain and LoRA-aware baselines and holds up well on new tasks.
arxiv-2603-26399: Li and Yang investigate sums and products of infinite multiple zeta-star values with restricted indices. These values extend classic multiple zeta values by allowing equality in their defining sums. Like continued fractions, the theory lets any real number above one be written as a unique infinite zeta-star value. The authors study how such values behave under addition and multiplication. Drawing on continued fractions and Cantor set ideas, they propose conjectures about algebraic points among these values.
arxiv-2603-26499: Hambardzumyan and co-authors present AIRA_2, a system that attacks three bottlenecks in AI research agents. Single-GPU synchronous runs limit how many trials an agent can test. Validation-based picking can also overfit as searches run long, and fixed one-turn operators cap what search can do. AIRA_2 answers with an asynchronous multi-GPU worker pool, a hidden consistent scoring protocol, and ReAct agents that debug as they go. On MLE-bench-30 it reaches a mean percentile rank of 81.5% at 24 hours, ahead of the best rival.
arxiv-2603-26599: An and co-authors present VGGRPO, a post-training method that makes generated videos hold their geometry over time. Large video diffusion models look strong yet often warp scene shape across frames. Their Latent Geometry Model links video latents to a geometry foundation model, reading scene shape without decoding to pixels. A 4D rebuild skill lets the rewards cover moving scenes, not just still ones. Group Relative Policy Optimization then trains with rewards for camera smoothness and geometric fit, all inside latent space.
arxiv-2603-26799: Huang proposes Gaussian Joint Embeddings, a probabilistic route to self-supervised representation learning. Standard predictive methods can collapse toward average answers when a task has many valid outputs. His method models the joint density of context and target codes instead of predicting one from the other. Closed-form conditional inference then replaces the black-box predictor, with honest uncertainty attached. He names a failure mode of naive batch training, the Mahalanobis Trace Trap, and offers fixes from prototypes to a Monte Carlo memory bank.
arxiv-2603-26899: Tonnesen and co-authors simulate star-forming gas clouds blown by a hot cluster wind. Ram pressure strips gas from satellite galaxies, and stars can form inside the stripped tails. A fireball model predicts young stars farthest from the disk. The team's clouds, with star formation included, do show age gradients in that direction. But compression, shredding, and gravity make the gradients strongly nonmonotonic. Stars form at mixed heights and speeds at the same time. The clearest fireball patterns come from clouds shredded fast.
arxiv-2603-27299: Chen and co-authors extend a declarative routing language from single LLM requests to full agent workflows. The Semantic Router DSL already routes inference traffic from one source file. Its signals cover similarity, private data detection, and jailbreak scoring. It now emits verified decision nodes for agent tools like LangGraph. It also emits Kubernetes policies, network configs, and protocol gates. A threshold change flows from gateway to infrastructure in one step. Four pillars frame the design: auditability, cost, verifiability, and tunability.
arxiv-2603-27699: Simm and co-authors add trust intervals to cloud process emulators. Conformal prediction gives valid intervals for any regressor. It needs no model changes and little compute. Six microphysical rates from the ICON model serve as targets. Split conformal and conformalized quantile methods face off. Both yield calibrated, sharp intervals on average. Quantile-based intervals stay steadier across wide value ranges. That steadiness suits climate variables best.
arxiv-2603-27899: Kousek and Saavedra-Araya prove that Furstenberg systems are unique up to isomorphism. A bounded function on a semigroup spawns such a system. The system encodes how the function behaves over time. Any two such systems match in structure. That mirrors a known result for the measurable case. Tests say when two sets share isomorphic systems. Minimal systems mark a subclass of syndetic sets. Recurrence in dynamics gains a new description.
arxiv-2603-28499: Mohri and four co-authors ask when a next-token predictor can drive good choices against an adversary. The induced player best-responds to the model's forecast of the foe's moves. With an unbounded context window, every action distribution sits very close to one that yields low regret, so cheap fixes always work. With a bounded window, as in real transformers, some distributions stay far from all low-regret ones. They also show transformer layers can carry out the fix.
arxiv-2603-28599: Beyer and Nunes present the East Lansing Model, a global optical potential with quantified uncertainty. It covers neutron and proton projectiles and adds a new form for the neutron-proton asymmetry term. The goal is better extrapolation away from stable nuclei. Calibration uses angular data for spherical targets with mass at least 40, at 10 to 100 MeV. Adding charge-exchange data alone changed little for stable nuclei. A new parametrization lets the model encode neutron skins through the asymmetry term. Extrapolation toward the driplines gave smaller uncertainties than other global models.
arxiv-2603-28699: Li and co-authors report GRB 160425A, a gamma-ray burst with two sub-bursts four minutes apart. Bursts are usually classed as short merger events or long collapsar events. The first sub-burst looks short-like by duration, hardness, variability, and spectral traits. The second looks long-like by the same standard diagnostics. Nearly all prompt-emission tests agree on that split. One event thus carries both merger and collapsar signatures. The authors say this challenges current progenitor frameworks.
arxiv-2603-28799: Borges and Campos link tritium breeding and heat removal in lithium-based fusion systems in one compact model. Lithium both breeds tritium in blankets and removes heat in liquid-metal parts. Past work treated neutron behavior, jet thermal response, and control as separate layers. They join nuclear cross-section data, a reduced jet model, and an operator form of feedback control. A PID controller embeds in a family of Bessel-type operators acting on tritium tracking error. The system is a conceptual reduced-order demonstration, not a full reactor design.
arxiv-2603-29099: Molinares and co-authors show how to build arrays of phonon lasers. A phonon laser is a device with self-sustained, coherent vibration. Past designs lacked scale and tied all units to one shared field. Their design drives each unit locally inside a spin chain. They derive the resonance conditions for the switch to coherent motion. Switching one coupling on or off lases a chosen site on demand. The array also syncs on its own near resonance.
arxiv-2603-29199: Mankodiya and co-authors introduce AEC-Bench, a benchmark for agents in architecture, engineering, and construction. Tasks require reading drawings and reasoning across sheets. Others need project-level coordination. The report explains the benchmark's goals, task taxonomy, and scoring protocol. Baseline runs cover several domain-specific model harnesses. Some tools and harness choices improved results across all models tested. The dataset, harness, and code are released openly for reuse. The license is Apache 2.
arxiv-2603-29299: McCulloch answers a question about automorphisms of finite abelian groups. The question asks whether every positive rational number can arise as a certain ratio. The ratio compares the size of a group's automorphism group with the group itself. His answer is no. He shows the denominator of any such ratio must be squarefree. His argument uses coprime numerator and denominator. He also shows no odd prime can equal that ratio. The note settles the question with two clean restrictions.
arxiv-2603-29399: Zanoli and co-authors revisit a benchmark for building data pipelines with AI agents. On ELT-Bench, agents first looked weak at extract-load-transform work. Newer models solved the extraction and loading stages. The team then audited the benchmark itself for quality flaws. Most failed transformation tasks held benchmark-side errors. Rigid scripts, vague specs, and wrong ground truth penalized correct outputs. Their corrected version, ELT-Bench-Verified, uses refined scoring logic. Scores rose sharply from the correction alone.
arxiv-2603-29599: Tegomo Chiogo and co-authors test Kondo scaling in the heavy fermion compound CeSi2. Many 4f-electron systems follow Kondo scaling set by one characteristic temperature. Surface-sensitive tools limit how fully that scaling can be checked. The team uses bulk-sensitive resonant X-ray scattering across temperatures. Single-impurity Anderson model calculations run alongside. As temperature rises, the f0 state occupancy falls and another state gains weight. The data match the model well. The results show the Kondo singlet breaking down with heat.
arxiv-2603-29699: Gay and co-authors study gravitational wave turbulence inside the Hadad-Zakharov metric. The metric is set by four functions that must meet seven Einstein equations. Whether those equations can hold together was overlooked until now. The authors argue they can, in the weakly nonlinear regime, under set conditions. A new GPU code, TIGER, runs direct simulations of the setup. The runs show a dual cascade of energy and wave action. A Kolmogorov-Zakharov spectrum appears for the wave action. Caution is urged, since meeting all equations precisely is hard.
arxiv-2603-29899: Yamada and co-authors map gas around the N113 star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud. ALMA and APEX carbon monoxide data reveal two filaments about ten parsecs long. The filaments meet in a V shape and host massive young stars in bound dense gas. Wider hydrogen data show two velocity streams split by over 40 kilometers per second. One stream sits inside a cavity in the other. The team argues a collision 1.3 million years ago triggered the cloud's birth.
arxiv-2603-29999: Aguzzi and co-authors present Phyelds, a Python library for aggregate programming. That field-based style coordinates swarms across sensor networks, robots, and IoT. Existing tools live in Scala, C++, or other languages, not Python. Data science work, though, centers on Python's ecosystem. Phyelds gives a full field calculus engine with a Pythonic interface. Its design plugs into Python machine learning tools. Examples span classic coordination patterns and federated learning. It also links with a multi-agent learning simulator.
arxiv-2604-00099: Ajjath, Chaubey, and Shao sharpen theoretical predictions for light-by-light scattering, one of the earliest forecasts of quantum electrodynamics. Interest revived after its observation at the Large Hadron Collider. They refine two-loop amplitudes with full fermion-mass dependence through high- and low-energy expansions and add Coulomb resummation near threshold. The result is state-of-the-art Standard Model cross sections plus LbLatNLO, a new event generator for Monte Carlo studies of the process.
arxiv-2604-00299: Temkulkiat and four colleagues mine 591 pull requests with 5,027 Python files from three AI agents, mapping constructs onto six levels from A1 to C2 with pycefr. Over 90 percent of agent constructs are Basic level (A1 and A2), with under 1 percent at Mastery (C2), and agent and human requests share a similar profile. High-proficiency agent code comes mostly from feature additions and bug fixes. Agent code is generally readable with basic Python skills, though some tasks demand advanced skill to review and maintain.
arxiv-2604-00699: Zádor and colleagues propose a framework for buses and trains in the 15-minute city model. The 15-minute city counters car use by pushing walking and cycling to shops and open areas, but poor edges pose problems. Public transport gets little attention despite its far-off role. Open data comparisons of Helsinki, Madrid, and Budapest show mixed-mode travel raises amenity access and social-spatial mixing within a 15-minute reach. Edge areas gain mixing promise from fast radial lines, yet such lines alone do not improve amenity access.
arxiv-2604-00799: Khangaonkar, Rad, and Pirsiavash test whether multimodal language models can spot objects that break 3D motion consistency between two views of one scene. They build realistic inconsistent image pairs from multi-view scenes at scale, then measure models against human observers. Leading models fall well short of people and vary widely across scene attributes, showing a fragile, incomplete grasp of 3D structure.
arxiv-2604-00999: Mäkinen works out how simple semiclassical states for uniform, direction-free spatial shapes evolve in quantum-reduced loop gravity, using a deparametrized dynamics where a reference matter field serves as relational time. His states sit in a spin network graph's Hilbert space, with just one six-valent vertex. He finds the quantum motion broadly tracks the semiclassical effective motion of such a universe within the numerical approximation's range. In particular, a shrinking shape hits a dynamical bounce, halting shrinkage and turning it into growth.
arxiv-2604-01299: Backhoff, Beiglböck, Bifronte and Ley study the martingale Schrödinger bridge, a martingale transport plan between two probability laws in convex order. They show the build extends to any dimension and admits several matching characterizations. Its continuous-time version is the martingale with set marginals. It minimizes a weighted quadratic energy measuring the gap from Brownian motion. In the irreducible case, this bridge coincides with the Föllmer martingale. More broadly, they relate it to a variational problem over base measures and to the dual weak optimal transport problem.
arxiv-2604-01499: Hoy and colleagues compare evolution methods and Group Relative Policy Optimization across single tasks and task chains. Evolution strategies match or beat GRPO in accuracy and stay competitive when iteration budget is capped. Despite similar task results, the methods produce different model updates: evolution methods make larger changes and broader off-task KL drift, while GRPO makes smaller, more local updates. The evolution-strategy and GRPO results are linearly connected with no loss barrier, even though their update directions are nearly orthogonal. They develop a theory for the method.
arxiv-2604-01599: Nguyen and colleagues propose ByteRover, an agent-native memory system where the same language model that reasons also curates, structures, and retrieves knowledge. Others treat memory as an external service, handing storage to chunking, embedding, and graph extraction. Retrieval uses five tiers resolving most queries in under 100 ms without model calls, escalating to agentic reasoning only for novel questions. ByteRover stores knowledge in a Context Tree laid out as Domain, Topic, Subtopic, and Entry. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval, ByteRover reaches top accuracy on LoCoMo and competitive results on LongMemEval.
arxiv-2604-01699: Bini and Di Russo compute the gravitational wave signal for a two-body system in radial fall, using multipolar methods at 2.5 post-Newtonian accuracy.
