At that level a reaction force from emitted waves appears, altering the fall and producing bremsstrahlung radiation. They tally all emissions: energy, angular momentum, which vanishes, and linear momentum. They also tally nonlocal inertial forces entering at the next order, 4.5 post-Newtonian, in the center of mass, paving the way for sharper future work.
arxiv-2604-02099: Boyd, Bregman and Steinebrunner study moduli spaces of reducible manifolds via a prime decomposition fibre sequence. Their splitting map yields the sequence, with fibre described as a colimit of configuration spaces of handle attachments. The fibre proves equivalent to a finite, connected cell complex, making the sequence a useful tool. The authors show it by computing the cohomology ring of a moduli space.
arxiv-2604-02199: Das and Pal build a unified frame for best sync in directed multiplex networks of phase oscillators. A synchrony alignment function blends structure and dynamics of each directed layer. From it they derive two frequency sets: one giving perfect sync at a set coupling strength despite phase lag, and one giving the best sync across a wide coupling range. Tests on directed duplex networks show both sets beat standard choices. Link rewiring and frequency swapping add further gains, and optimized networks show clear frequency degree patterns.
arxiv-2604-02399: Zhang and Liu synthesize safe Rust code from public API signatures with a new Pushdown Colored Petri Net. Token colors encode dynamic resource states plus a scope level for each borrow lifetime region, while the pushdown stack tracks entering and leaving lifetime parameters. A transition fires only when type matching, interface obligations and required resource states all hold. Bisimulation theory proves the net rules match compile time checks for ownership, borrowing and lifetime. A synthesis tool built on the net produces code that tests show is all correct.
arxiv-2604-02499: Hawthorne and four colleagues introduce C2DTD, a short code for two-dimensional carbon nets ranging from clean graphene to sheets full of defects. The code blends local shapes, a radial pattern and ring layout into one fixed-length vector that stays easy to read. In tests it predicts well from small datasets, and ring layout turns out to drive energy most, above all where missing atoms reshape the net.
arxiv-2604-03199: Ilić and colleagues show that fine-tuning leaves a learnable fingerprint of memorization in language models, detectable across model families. Their classifier, trained only on transformers, transfers untouched to Mamba, RWKV-4, and RecurrentGemma, beating its held-out transformer scores. The shared thread is gradient descent on cross-entropy loss, and the method also transfers to code despite training only on prose.
arxiv-2604-03299: Liu and colleagues build MoViD, a viewpoint-invariant pose estimator that separates viewpoint from motion in 3D human pose estimation. A view estimator predicts viewpoint from joint relationships, and an orthogonal projection module disentangles motion and view features with physics-grounded contrastive alignment. Tests show errors down more than 24 percent against leading methods, with real-time inference at 15 frames per second on edge devices.
arxiv-2604-03399: Thomas, Shivakumar, and Velni extend impulse-to-peak optimal control from ordinary differential equations to linear partial differential equations. Using the partial integral equation form as a state-space model plus Lyapunov methods, they turn the response problem into a convex optimization with proven norm bounds. Strong duality then yields a direct state-feedback control, shown on several examples.
arxiv-2604-03599: Seitz, Schmitt, and Schiffler present a method to pick a single best guess from a bagging predictor set. It uses KDE in curved fitting with neural networks, plus a quality yardstick called the Bagging Score. The approach beats the common mean or middle value and tops error rankings in matchups with several curved fitting methods, without tuning or feature picking.
arxiv-2604-03799: Zhiwei Zheng and colleagues built MoScale, a text-to-motion generator that works scale by scale instead of token by token. Global meaning enters at the coarsest scale and sharpens step by step, giving a causal hierarchy that suits long motion better than flat next-token prediction. Cross-scale and in-scale refinement steps steady the model when text-motion data are scarce. MoScale reached leading text-to-motion scores, trains efficiently, and generalizes to new motion and editing tasks without further tuning.
arxiv-2604-04199: Simon Roth measured how badly four classes of data leakage distort machine learning scores across 2,047 tabular datasets, plus a test on 129 temporal sets. Estimation leakage from fitting scalers on full data proved tiny, with all nine conditions shifting AUC by no more than 0.005 either way. Selection leakage from peeking and seed cherry-picking proved substantial, matching about 90 percent noise exploitation that inflates stated scores. Memorization grew with model capacity, while edge leakage stayed invisible under random cross-validation, inverting the textbook emphasis.
arxiv-2604-04599: Carneiro and three colleagues present LP-GEMM, a GEMM kernel split that lets packing layout carry across sequential GEMMs. BLAS libraries tune each GEMM call alone, yet the API forces each call to pack inputs and restore outputs to canonical layout. LP-GEMM drops needless repacking while keeping BLAS meaning correct at the boundaries. Tests on x86 and RISC-V show mean speedups of 2.25x over OpenBLAS for sequential GEMMs. A standalone C++ Llama-3.2 inference path built from BLAS GEMM calls shows the approach works beyond microbenchmarks.
arxiv-2604-04699: Teh, Thenabadu, Drummond and Reid run Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen correlations for a two-mode squeezed state to test ideas of the homodyne current from a Schrödinger equation. They find the stochastic term for the current in the broad-band limit. Stratonovich rather than Ito noise agrees with tests. The authors show this matters for readout noise and errors in quantum devices. By watching Schrödinger trajectories as readout settings change, they propose a modern gedanken test. There, one measures position and momenta at once, one direct, the other indirect.
arxiv-2604-04799: Hakimoglu-Brown gives a new integration route to special values of hypergeometric 2F1 series with rational parameters and argument. Such series rarely admit evaluations in gamma values, apart from cases at plus or minus one and one half. He applies the route to a 2F1 at one quarter due to Gosper, later studied by Vidunas, Ebisu, and Zudilin. It evaluates a series whose convergence rate is the square of 172872 over 185039. Among strange 2F1 evaluations, the new series seems to carry the largest numerator and denominator in its argument.
arxiv-2604-05099: Namugwanya builds and tests persistent MPI RMA variants of Alltoallv, a collective call central to many HPC apps with uneven message sizes. The variants use fence and lock sync, separating a one-time setup phase from per-iteration runs to reuse data and window state across repeated epochs. Tests on LLNL's Dane machine show the fence variant always beats the baseline for large messages, cutting runtime by up to 44 percent. At 448 processes it runs 38 percent faster, with scaling rising as process counts grow.
arxiv-2604-05199: Niewinski and Johnson derive a novel approach to approximating Fourier transforms, focusing on 2D ring-like functions. The problem reduces to Hankel transforms of each angular mode, approximated with the focal expansion. The single approximation stays accurate from small to large frequencies, bridging regimes where expansions are individually reliable. Examples show the leading focal term gives an accurate global approximation for many functions. Its utility is shown via the interferometric response for toy models of a black hole's photon ring, relevant to the Black Hole Explorer.
arxiv-2604-05399: Ahn and five colleagues automate formal software proofs by mining structural patterns from proof states instead of retrieving surface-similar text. Their PROMISE system searches over proof-state transitions, reusing and adapting compatible proof fragments as it goes. On the seL4 microkernel benchmark it beats earlier systems by up to 26 points, a relative gain of 186 percent, while holding steady across different model backends.
arxiv-2604-05599: Spooren and three colleagues layer post-quantum cryptography over quantum key distribution for long-distance trusted-node networks. Hop tunnels run WireGuard with rotating pre-shared keys from the QKD interface, while Rosenpass adds end-to-end post-quantum exchange without touching deployed devices. Lab and simulated tests show steady multi-hop operation, small footprint, and fail-safe behavior.
arxiv-2604-05899: Ben Khelil and four colleagues release FRENCH-YMCA, a French corpus for kids and teens with 39,200 texts and over 22 million words. Varied sources, steady grammar and spelling, and open access set it apart. The corpus helps language models learn how young people write and speak, backing digital tools that fit each age group.
arxiv-2604-06199: Manik and Wang ask whether a synthetic society can regulate itself, studying 39,026 posts and 5,712 comments from 14,490 OpenClaw agents on Moltbook. They score directive language with Directive Intensity, a lexicon-based gauge of instructional phrasing. Directive posts appear in about 18 percent of the archive, and corrective replies grow more likely as posts grow more directive. That link survives a mixed-effects logistic model accounting for nesting. Thread patterns suggest negative feedback after the first correction. The findings point to corrective signaling in this collective.
arxiv-2604-06399: Pal, Rai, and Kumbhar report a calibration instability in new Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope Band 4. Tests showed cross-hand phase varies by source, breaking calibration sharing. Checks traced the fault to the Quadrature Hybrid polarizer. Skipping it in seven dishes cut leakage from 10 to 15 percent to 2 to 5 percent, and leakage to under a fifth of a percent, calming phases. For DA 240, the fixed system recovered the expected 25 degree rotation, which the polarizer system failed to match. The results blame the Quadrature Hybrid polarizer and support linear feeds.
arxiv-2604-06499: Pareek and three colleagues develop private equivalence testing for settings where standard tests risk leaks. Privacy matters for surveys, big-tech data, and especially healthcare, where hospital comparisons and lab calibrations need private statistics. Standard equivalence tests for proportions or means can leak. The team builds DP-TOST, a unified framework for equivalence testing of means and proportions. Simulations and real applications show nominal type-I error control with power near the non-private version as budget or sample size grows. That offers a reliable framework for high-stakes fields.
arxiv-2604-06599: Li, Akil, and Bertino probe whether malware detectors that adapt to shifting data can also resist attack. The undefended AdvDA system fell completely to white-box PGD attacks and partly to black-box MalGuise binary mutations. Their retraining framework, tuned on adversarially altered inputs, cut PGD success to about 3 percent and also sharply reduced MalGuise success. Yet the best recipe differed by threat. Source training proved vital against PGD but harmful against MalGuise, and defenses did not transfer across threats.
arxiv-2604-06899: Babu and four colleagues study data leakage in car perception teams. Leakage, the stray transfer of information between train and test sets, threatens trust in safety-critical car systems. Ten interviews with design, building, and checking engineers show knowledge common yet split by role. Machine learning staff frame it as splitting or checks; design and checking roles frame it as sample fit and scenario coverage. Spotting it leans on generic checks and odd results, stopping it on shared know-how, and the authors call leakage control a team coordination problem.
arxiv-2604-07299: Majhi, Mondal, and Agnihotri test location-based games as a way to keep community healthcare workers in India engaged in collecting child health data. Accurate anthropometric records matter for planning care, but existing platforms lose engagement over time and place, leaving patchy, outdated maps. A co-design exercise produced hotspot and density maps plus a game-based collection method, trialled with two groups of 94 workers each. The game approach improved measuring efficiency significantly and beat the standard method on engagement and retention.
arxiv-2604-07699: Crosby and five colleagues run a pilot study on smoke smell in a virtual reality game for wildfire evacuation training. Eighteen people split evenly into smoke and control groups completed the same evacuation task, with post-task surveys on perceived preparedness and overall experience. People in the smoke group reported far higher immersion than those in the control group. Across both groups, people felt more prepared for real-world wildfire evacuations after the experience.
arxiv-2604-07899: Ramaschi, Paolone, and Leva open a study of game-theoretic control for electric vehicle charging stations with the incentive-design part. Large stations prove too big for centralized real-time dispatch, and decentralized control without incentives misaligns drivers' goals. The team puts a decentralized algorithm in a hierarchical three-layer energy management system as the real-time layer. A centralized approach sets the dispatch plan and refines it daily, while the game-theoretic layer handles real-time control. SG-ADMM designs incentives while managing power dispatch in a distributed way.
arxiv-2604-08199: Qi and three colleagues propose MobiWM, a mobile network world model for mobile traffic outlook. Mobile traffic forecast is basic yet hard for radio network planning and tuning. Standard models mostly learn static long-term time patterns and miss dynamics under network-setting changes. MobiWM treats cell traffic as states and antenna settings as actions. It joins factorized space-time models with mixed outside context joined by shared spatial meaning. Its learned action-state steps allow repeat rollout over set paths for what-if planning.
arxiv-2604-08399: Shehabeldin and six colleagues review tunnel junctions made from atomically thin van der Waals layers whose current can be steered by light. Light pushes charge carriers out of balance and opens paths that stay closed in the dark, giving electrical access to fast dynamics and collective behavior in quantum materials. The review covers photodetection, light emission, sensing, and memory, and looks ahead to twist resolved spectroscopy, moiré ferroelectricity, and scalable computing and sensing designs.
arxiv-2604-08499: Geng and four colleagues offer PIArena, a single extensible platform for judging prompt injection attacks and defenses across tasks and benchmarks. Its dynamic attack adapts injected prompts from defense feedback, exposing weak spots in current defenses. Evaluations find limited generalization across tasks, vulnerability to adaptive attacks, and deep trouble when an injected task matches the target task, showing why unified testing matters for security claims.
arxiv-2604-08699: Qi and four colleagues show sideways heat flow inside a crater can drive a positive YORP torque on asteroids, spinning them up. Three dimensional finite element models of a round crater on a spherical asteroid find crater torques always positive, pushing spin axes toward tilt rest points at 0, 90, or 180 degrees. For small craters the effect reaches roughly 10 to 100 percent of normal YORP torque, possibly explaining why positive spin speedups lead surveys.
arxiv-2604-08899: Ren extends the theory of distribution-dependent stochastic equations to cases with singular interactions. In these systems, each particle's motion depends on the spread of the whole crowd, and earlier work had settled well-posedness, chaos propagation, and ergodicity. Ren derives Bismut-type formulas for the derivative of the solution, a tool linking small shifts in the starting spread to shifts in solutions. The new formulas extend the version known before only for drifts differentiable in the Lions sense.
arxiv-2604-09199: Sengupta, Kuş, Li, and Zachow recover the pose of a known 3D shape from its plain silhouettes alone, with global optimality. Their method uses silhouette area continuity as rotation varies, storing precomputed signatures as a response surface over rotation space. Querying that surface prunes the rotation search sharply, and fitted ellipse ratios add a second global shape cue. It needs no point correspondences and works for any shape, beating comparable methods on synthetic and real examples.
arxiv-2604-09399: Sneppen and colleagues report Paschen jumps in a subset of Little Red Dots, broad-line sources at high redshift. Little Red Dots were first spotted by compact shapes, red colors, and strong Balmer breaks, with debated optical-to-near-infrared continua. The Paschen jumps fit free-bound recombination to hydrogen level three, with Paschen and Brackett shapes matching minimally reddened low-temperature gas. Extreme hydrogen-alpha widths and the tight link between line and continuum follow naturally from recombination, giving an upper limit on direct accretion and stellar-atmosphere contributions.
arxiv-2604-09499: Sivashangaran and four colleagues teach a race car to drive without a prebuilt map. Their method uses deep reinforcement learning shaped by vehicle physics. It neither copies human drivers nor piles up simulated crashes. The network reads depth-sensor patterns to infer time-optimal and overtaking moves. It runs on less than 1 percent of the computation of cloning or model-based rivals. On scaled hardware and unfamiliar tracks, it beats human demonstrations by 12 percent.
arxiv-2604-09599: Loreti, Leone, and Borghesi add a machine-learning duration predictor to a high-performance-computing workload scheduler, since good scheduling hinges on knowing job lengths in advance. Users rarely supply reliable estimates, so the predictor fills the gap from workload traces. Evaluated on traces from a Tier-0 supercomputer, the enhanced scheduler cuts mean waiting time across all jobs by around 11 percent. Shorter waits mean better service for users and faster turnaround for the system.
arxiv-2604-09899: Hare and Mendivil determine the range of almost sure large Phi-dimensions for random Moran measures. These dimensions tune a range of depths in scale, giving fine local shape detail; one well-known large Phi-dimension example is the quasi-Assouad dimension. Results cover both cases: probability weights depending on scaling factors, and weights independent of them. In the independent case, a gap usually appears between the set's dimension and the attainable upper and lower dimensions. The results also give the almost sure dimensions of the underlying random Moran set.
arxiv-2604-10099: Hewage, Chakkravarthy, and Abeysekara test error mitigation for variational quantum circuits that solve partial differential equations on noisy hardware. They cover heat, Burgers, and shallow-water flows. Zero-noise extrapolation cuts error by 82 to 96 percent at low noise. Circuits held to equation residuals keep 25 to 47 percent higher fidelity than free ones at moderate noise. Probabilistic error cancellation is near-exact for few gates, but its sampling cost blows up fast and turns impractical beyond about 60 gates.
arxiv-2604-10199: Loi and Moustakas build tired human motion with FatigueFusion, a deep-learning design fusing fatigue traits in latent space. Tired-motion making remains rare. Unlike methods that merely imitate built-up fatigue effects, their method imposes each subject's own fatigue traits on fresh motions. Physics-aware neural network methods mimic fatigue strength. Working on fresh joint angles and control settings in latent space, the system needs no fatigue input data. It supports fatigue profile transfer and fusion, plus lifelike fatigue in film and simulation.
arxiv-2604-10399: Araujo builds object classes in Tcl from plain lists and dicts, with no added frame. His VOO objects are plain Tcl lists with copy on write care, so no destructor chore remains. Creation runs 7 to 18 times faster than TclOO, and memory use drops 4 to 6 times. A C++ path speeds field access further and trims memory more, keeping the same Tcl call style. Cross version checks show the plain design ages better as the interpreter grows.
arxiv-2604-10599: Alenezi asks whether software craft must bend around agent made code. Machine written code now floods in, breaking the old manual authorship model. He weighs four fronts: engineer roles, checking as bottleneck, output effects, and field wide fallout. Code turns from a scarce crafted good into a plentiful throwaway item. The fix centers orchestration of agent teams, strict verification, and planned human machine teamwork.
arxiv-2604-10799: Ociepa and four colleagues advance Polish language modeling through tokenizer tuning in the Bielik v3 7B and 11B models. One-size-fits-all tokenizers miss Polish word-shape nuances, raising token counts and running costs while shrinking usable context windows. The report details the move from Mistral token sets to a dedicated Polish-optimized vocabulary. It covers FOCUS-based vector setup and a multi-stage training plan. Post-training tuning uses supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and group-based policy optimization with reward checks.
arxiv-2604-10899: Nguyen asks when finite Gaussian mixture models can approximate a target density in Kullback-Leibler divergence. He isolates one mechanism behind several necessary-and-sufficient claims. Any density approximated this way must have finite second moment. Sufficiency needs mixtures whose likelihood ratios converge pointwise with uniformly integrable log-ratios. He checks this for finite log-moment densities and a support-aware class allowing zero regions, then gives counterexamples showing neither class contains the other.
arxiv-2604-10999: Petrova, Chen, and Soljačić present TraversalBench, a benchmark for exact visual path following under controlled conditions. Each instance holds a polyline with a unique start mark and labeled vertices, and models must recover the ordered sequence. It balances self-intersection counts, tortuosity, vertex counts, and nearby distracting lines. It limits reliance on text reading or world knowledge. Self-intersections dominate difficulty. Performance holds steady before the first crossing, then drops sharply at the correct continuation. A reading-order test reveals a consistent left-to-right bias.
arxiv-2604-11099: Gopinath and three colleagues map stacking work function and photoresponse in CVD molybdenum disulfide bilayers. Stacking order in these bilayers controls symmetry and layer interactions. This offers a route to tune electronic properties for uses. The work function is key for device performance, yet stacking effects on it remain poorly understood. Using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy, the authors probe surface potential and determine the work function of AA-prime and AB bilayers. The work function grows with layer count in both stackings, with a larger AB difference reflecting stronger coupling.
arxiv-2604-11199: Greaves gives an explicit deterministic recipe for drawing exact Beta variables with a shape pair summing to one. It uses a fixed number of uniform draws and only basic operations. The build, an extended one-liner in Devroye's sense, extends as corollaries to Beta pairs with a smaller shape below one and to Gamma shapes below one. Dirichlet vectors whose parts all sit below one follow too.
arxiv-2604-11399: Fu and four colleagues restore time reasoning in video models with MERIT, a merging framework. Tuning can weaken time reasoning even when visual evidence is read correctly, but some competence survives in the earlier checkpoint. MERIT assigns each attention layer a vision- or language-led mix, searched with a covariance strategy under a perception limit. Across three model families and five benchmarks it improves reasoning in all 15 tests while preserving time perception. Recipes from 232 test examples transfer to unseen benchmarks at gains up to 27.8 percent.
arxiv-2604-11699: Xue and four colleagues improve reach in turning legal cases into logic formulas with diverse few-shot learning. Logic-based reasoning fine-tunes models to map cases into formulas, but annotated training data are scarce. Legal2LogicICL enables in-context learning via retrieval, balancing exemplar mix at semantic levels. It also cuts entity bias, where long entity mentions swamp semantics and obscure legal patterns. The framework builds few-shot demos for logical rule making without extra training, plus a Legal2Proleg dataset linking cases with PROLEG formulas.
arxiv-2604-11899: Carniani and thirty-three colleagues present JWST spectra of JADES-GS-z14-0, a cosmic-dawn galaxy at redshift 14.18. A carbon emission line appears three times brighter in one dataset than the other, and shutter placement explains the gap: the glowing gas sits about 400 parsecs from the starlight. The gas spreads over at least 165 parsecs, and as an outflow it implies gas leaving at about 160 solar masses per year, four to fifteen times the star-formation rate. Such feedback, they argue, caps star-formation efficiency in massive haloes at or below 0.08.
arxiv-2604-12099: Rangreji, Zhong, and Field evaluate how document choice shapes query-focused text analysis, a missed methodological choice. They test seven methods, from random picks to hybrid retrieval, across four analysis methods — LDA, BERTopic, TopicGPT, and HiCode — over two datasets with 26 open-ended queries. Their guidance: semantic or hybrid retrieval are strong go-to defaults, avoiding weaker pitfalls and extra overhead from more complex ones. Overall, the framework makes data choice a method decision rather than a practical necessity, spurring new methods.
arxiv-2604-12599: Dino Conciatore and six colleagues map the full AI lifecycle onto national supercomputing. Pre-training put supercomputers at the heart of sovereign AI efforts. Fine-tuning and inference follow different operational patterns. They need heavy compute but use hardware unlike pre-training. The team presents a hybrid cloud-native platform at the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre. Diskless GPU nodes join virtualized commodity infrastructure under Kubernetes. Early work covers tuning pipelines and always-on inference services. The design offers a blueprint for AI Factory services on supercomputers.
arxiv-2604-12699: Rhyan Barrett and two colleagues screen fluorescent protein chromophores with a transferable model. Standard excited-state simulations cost too much for broad screening. Their X-MACE potential predicts energy maps, forces, and strengths. Hopping guided by curvature then enables efficient pathway screening. Green fluorescent protein variants show how small changes reshape relaxation. Tuning one pretrained model on fewer than 100 geometries per variant yields good dynamics. Crowding on the ring lowers twist barriers and speeds twisted intersections. Longer chains stabilize planar states, curb dark decay, and prolong fluorescence.
arxiv-2604-12999: Koo and five colleagues treat neural architecture discovery as hypothesis-driven science with HypoExplore, a system that proposes, builds, tests, and refines vision networks through evolutionary branching. A trajectory tree tracks each design's lineage while a memory bank updates confidence scores from experimental evidence. On CIFAR-10 the best design climbs from 18.91 percent to 94.11 percent accuracy, and the approach also reaches leading results on MedMNIST.
arxiv-2604-13099: Datta builds a Melnikov framework for the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation under weak deterministic and stochastic forcing. Treating the equation as a dynamic system of endless dimensions, she derives a measure of how stable and unstable manifolds of a homoclinic orbit split apart. Periodic forcing yields phase-linked crossings, while random forcing gives random splitting set by the adjoint solution, linking manifold theory to chaos in space and time.
arxiv-2604-13199: Lin and four colleagues simulate radiation flows of accretion onto a supermassive black hole. Mass enters at 10 Schwarzschild radii, with a black hole mass of 10 to the 7 solar masses. Reading mass inflow over time, they find oscillation signals whose frequencies match radial epicyclic frequencies beyond a critical radius of 3.8 Schwarzschild radii, the radius of maximum epicyclic frequency. They propose that maximum as a proxy for the observed oscillation rate, matching its mass pattern across active galactic nuclei and tidal disruption events.
arxiv-2604-13399: Nan Liu and three colleagues find conditions under which maximum score estimation for binary choice models reaches root-n convergence to a normal distribution. The classic maximum score estimator converges slower than root-n to an odd limit, a known practical and theoretical weakness. By using concave surrogate score functions, they achieve identification with a smooth criterion. They spell out the needed conditions in basic terms, and simulations back the root-n rate, normal limit, and standard inference.
arxiv-2604-13599: Fu and three colleagues prove an observability inequality for strongly coupled parabolic systems of two equations, where only one component is observed. Watching one part over time can still reveal the whole system. The catch is that the observed component can cancel itself out. High-frequency oscillations caused by the coupling make estimates at single moments fail. To get around this, they build a new integral interpolation bound based on a Remez-type result. With earlier strategies for measurable sets, it yields observability from space-time measurable sets.
arxiv-2604-13899: Hakimi and colleagues ask whether language models can take over the labelling step in active learning, using 278,000 German political TikTok comments on hate speech. Machine labels beat human-supervised classifiers while costing roughly a tenth as much, for one closed-source and one open-weight model. But the gain only appears when the task is split into two questions that mirror the human setup. Random sampling matched active learning, and people stay essential as evaluators.
arxiv-2604-14299: Zen and eight colleagues introduce the dynamic compass code on the heavy-hex lattice with a modest footprint and a demonstrated threshold. The code comes from a new measurement plan for syndrome extraction in the heavy-hex subsystem code. Different schedules trade protection between X and Z basis logical errors, and the new schedule gives the code a threshold for stability experiments. Finally, the authors show fault-tolerant logic through lattice surgery between code patches.
arxiv-2604-14499: Al-Karsani and Khanbaghi propose battery reserves for distributed frequency and voltage control in grid-forming microgrids. Earlier work covers secondary control with charge balancing for battery inverters, but links to tertiary control through service-based reserves and local adequacy stay largely open. Their plan sizes reserves for layered control, while a modified averaging control partly regulates them through consensus. Hardware-in-the-loop tests on a microgrid modeled on the IEEE 13-bus feeder show good control plus better power and energy sharing across droop and virtual-synchronous-machine inverters.
arxiv-2604-14699: Monaci and six colleagues mined the first FAST all-sky hydrogen survey release for galaxies that shine in hydrogen gas yet show no optical counterpart. Their cutoff sits near 28 magnitudes per square arcsecond in the DESI Legacy Survey. After vetting against catalogues, images, and interference, they kept 70 dark galaxy candidates within 50 megaparsecs, spread evenly with none inside the 11-megaparsec Local Volume. Compared with ordinary galaxies, they spin broader for a given hydrogen mass, giving follow-up observers a concrete target list.
arxiv-2604-14799: Madhusudhan, Yadav, and Lacoste introduce MM-AQA, a benchmark for multimodal refusal. It builds unanswerable cases from answerable ones by varying modality needs and evidence supply. Tests covered 2,079 samples, three models, and two multi-agent designs. Under standard prompting, the models rarely abstained, beaten by simple confidence baselines. Multi-agent designs abstained more at an accuracy cost, and sequential designs matched iterative ones, with miscalibration the bottleneck. Models refused absent evidence but reconciled degraded or contradictory evidence, so training to abstain is needed, not more prompting or agents.
arxiv-2604-14899: Tanabe studies the ODE/IM correspondence between C(2)-type linear problems and 2d N=1 superconformal field theories. On the ODE side, he adds a boundary condition for the conformal limit, diagonalizes the Lax operator, and extracts WKB periods and semi-local conserved quantities to tenth order. On the IM side, he computes eigenvalues of local integrals of motion on the cylinder in both Neveu-Schwarz and Ramond sectors. Comparison verifies to sixth order that WKB periods coincide with eigenvalues of local integrals of motion for highest-weight Neveu-Schwarz states.
arxiv-2604-15199: Tilquin reports recent LHCb searches for decays of third-generation particles that are rare or very rare. Such decays, including b-hadron and tau-lepton channels, probe physics beyond the Standard Model at scales direct searches cannot reach. Many carry predicted rates below current detector sensitivity, so the searches set the tightest limits to date. The proceedings cover first searches for several b-to-s tau and lepton-flavor channels, plus lepton-number-violating and loop-suppressed decays.
arxiv-2604-15399: Mondal and Choudhuri explore cosmic dynamics and structure growth in a modified gravity theory inspired by a generalized mass-to-horizon entropy relation. The entropic correction alters Friedmann expansion and perturbation growth, and the model passes diagnostic tests that falsify both flat and non-flat Lambda-CDM versions. It also reaches thermodynamic equilibrium in the far future, while massive halos grow scarcer and form later than in standard cosmology.
arxiv-2604-15599: Greenwood and Heitsch show that RNA ends sit nearer than random linear chains predict because branched structures pull their ends together. Using combinatorial branching models of growing complexity with multivariate analytic combinatorics, they fully characterize end-to-end distance means and variances. Shuffled structures match the theory, while known RNA structures share similar values but concentrate more tightly.
arxiv-2604-15999: Wang and eight colleagues untangle two electrical signals in magnetic insulators: spin pumping and spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance. In heavy-metal stacks, the two effects yield voltages of opposite signs, inviting ambiguous readings. Tests on platinum-capped garnet films in local and nonlocal devices show spin-wave character, damping, field direction, and device shape govern signal sign and size. They separate a spin pumping term from decaying spin waves and a weakly distance-dependent ST-FMR term from inductive coupling. Signal sign alone cannot be tied to magnon chirality.
arxiv-2604-16299: Feng and five co-authors present LaviGen, a design that reuses 3D generative models for autoregressive 3D layouts. Unlike methods that infer layouts from text, LaviGen works straight in native 3D space. It models geometric links and physical constraints among objects, yielding coherent, believable scenes. A 3D diffusion model blends scene, object, and instruction information. A two-part training trick boosts efficiency and spatial accuracy. On the LayoutVLM benchmark, it beats the state of the art by 19 percent in physical plausibility and runs 65 percent faster.
arxiv-2604-16399: Moreira proposes IACDM, an eight-phase method for AI-assisted software work that puts verification outside the generating model. Checking agents work at gates enforced by a state machine, so the generator can request progress but cannot grant it, while critique lenses attack artifacts. In a planned trial across twelve projects, every one of nineteen lenses caught a defect no other lens caught. Moreira stresses that this shows the method can be applied, not that it beats prompting, and writes the paper to invite refutation.
arxiv-2604-16599: Mantani and colleagues examine two-loop SMEFT equations for future collider studies. They solve the two-loop renormalization group equations with full numerical integration. Comparing one-loop and two-loop evolution matrices, they show two-loop terms change mixing patterns and remove zeroes seen at one loop. Fitting 61 Wilson coefficients at linear and quadratic level, they find non-negligible two-loop effects, especially for four-quark, top Yukawa and Higgs-gluon operators. Fits to scalar and fermion extensions of the Granada dictionary show percent-level sensitivity shifts.
arxiv-2604-17399: Zhuang, Zhang, Si, Zhou, and He address a blind spot in meta-reasoning for language models: methods act episode by episode and never bank reusable skills. Their Metacognitive Consolidation framework splits problem solving into reasoning, monitoring, and control roles, producing rich traces of each episode. A hierarchical, multi-timescale update then folds those traces into evolving meta-knowledge for future tasks. Experiments show steady gains across benchmarks and models, with performance rising as experience accumulates.
arxiv-2604-18099: Demeio proves solvable descent via a fibration theorem over quasi-trivial tori, following Harpaz and Wittenberg. The result answers the Grunwald problem for solvable groups positively, up to the necessary Brauer-Manin obstruction. It generalizes Shafarevich's answer to the Inverse Galois Problem and offers an alternative proof avoiding his shrinking procedure. Handling the obstruction means computing its triple variation on fiber grids, expressed through Redéi symbols, then applying a combinatorial principle to force vanishing in some fiber.
arxiv-2604-18199: Grantner, Sallinger, and Flechl build text embeddings from recurrent language models instead of transformers. Transformer embedders grow fast in compute and memory with input length, limiting long inputs. The authors tune Mamba2 models with a vertically chunked inference trick that holds memory flat once inputs pass the chunk size. Tests on Mamba2, RWKV, and xLSTM show strong accuracy with a much smaller footprint, making recurrent models a good efficient choice.
arxiv-2604-18299: Guiñazú, Juarez, Manasero, Neme, and Oviedo define pseudo-substitutable preferences, a maximal domain for pairwise stability in matching markets with contracts. Classical substitutability guarantees stable allocations but forbids complementarities between contracts. The new domain allows limited trade-offs while keeping stable outcomes, and the authors prove it is the largest such domain holding the older one. Stable matching thus reaches well beyond the older substitutable domain.
arxiv-2604-19699: Aroyehun, Lewandowsky, and Garcia measure epistemic orientation in parliamentary speech with an Evidence-Minus-Intuition score built from language model ratings and embedding-based similarity. Applying the score to 15 million speech segments from 1946 to 2025 across seven countries, they track how discourse leans toward evidence-based or intuition-based reasoning over time. They find the score rises with deliberative democracy and governance, tying evidence-leaning talk to democratic debate.
arxiv-2604-19899: Iturra-Bocaz and Galuscakova re-ran MetaRAG, a retrieval framework in which a language model critiques its own reasoning to judge when to stop searching. Their rerun confirms its edge over standard and reasoning-based baselines, but raw scores fall short of the first report. They blame closed-model updates, missing details, and unreleased prompts. Added rerankers lift scores a lot, and MetaRAG holds up better than the SIM-RAG critic method when more retrieval features join.
arxiv-2604-20499: Hu and three colleagues simulate a torn accretion disk reshaping the inner shadow of a Kerr black hole. When a tilted disk is ripped apart by frame-dragging, it splits into sub-disks. Their model traces light rays backward through that geometry. The torn layout erodes the shadow and creates split shadows, crescent shapes, and several orders of shadow rings. Those effects depend on the gap between sub-disks and outer tilt. Such patterns could diagnose torn disks, while warning that the inner shadow cannot test gravity theories.
arxiv-2604-20899: Walther and colleagues tackle the scale-up gap for metal-organic frameworks, sponge-like crystals whose plant-scale methods stay scattered across reports. They build ScaleMOF, a data set mined from papers, and tune large language models with a method that learns from known good cases alone. The tool ranks likely scale-up picks with 93.5 percent accuracy, giving makers a shortlist drawn from published work.
arxiv-2604-20999: The CMS Collaboration searches for dark matter made alongside a dark Higgs boson that decays to a bottom quark-antiquark pair, using proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. Data from the CMS detector at the CERN LHC in 2016 to 2018 give 138 inverse femtobarns. The signal is large missing transverse momentum plus a resonant mass bump in the bottom-quark pair. No excess appears, so upper limits at 95 percent confidence are set, excluding mediator masses up to 4.5 TeV for a 50 GeV dark Higgs, the tightest limits to date for these masses.
arxiv-2604-21699: Duits, El Moutaouakil, and Malavolta test whether large language models can help developers understand ROS2 robot software architectures, which link thousands of components in a decentralised way. They put 1,230 architecture questions about three ROS2 systems to nine models, checking answers against ground truth from running and monitoring the systems. Nearly all answers were right, averaging 98.22 percent, though the hardest system produced most errors.
arxiv-2604-21799: Xiao, Yang, and Meng tackle H2/H-infinity control for linear stochastic systems where the controller sees only an observation process, not the full state. The design balances H2 performance against H-infinity robustness under worst-case disturbances, framed as a game between two players. Kalman filtering yields the best filter equation. A Stochastic Bounded Real Lemma gives exact conditions for robustness. Nash equilibrium existence links to whether cross-coupled Riccati equations can be solved. A drone example shows the approach.
arxiv-2604-21899: Chen and 22 colleagues track how Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate thin films become superconducting. They tune strain and oxygen content independently in nickelate films, using X-ray absorption and resonant scattering. Under both tunings, spectral weight moves from an Upper Hubbard peak to an oxygen 2pz peak, while the nickel 3dz2 orbital becomes more itinerant. As itinerancy grows, long-range spin-density-wave order is suppressed, competing with superconductivity, while short-range magnons persist damped with unchanged bandwidth. Strain and oxygenation thus drive the films toward superconductivity through delocalisation.
arxiv-2604-21999: Sapunov studies learned memory tokens for a Universal Transformer with Adaptive Computation Time on Sudoku-Extreme. Memory tokens are necessary: no configuration without them reaches non-trivial performance. The token count has a sharp threshold: T=0 always fails and T=8 reliably succeeds, with a plateau at T=8-32 and a dilution boundary at T=64. Sapunov also identifies a router initialization trap causing most training runs to fail: default zero-bias and Graves' positive bias both settle into a shallow halt equilibrium. Inverting the bias to -3 eliminates the failure mode.
arxiv-2604-22099: Amate and five colleagues test how five dimensionality-reduction methods affect four clustering algorithms. The reduction methods are PCA, Kernel PCA, VAE, Isomap, and MDS; the clustering methods are k-means, agglomerative hierarchical clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and OPTICS. Quality is judged with the Adjusted Rand Index, weighing results with and without reduction at set levels, including k-1 and 25 and 50 percent of the starting dimensions. Their findings stress careful choice of both method and reduction level, fitted to data shape and the clustering algorithm in use.
arxiv-2604-22199: Su offers an autonomous closed-loop learning framework for robots facing new tasks. The framework first checks the local store for a reusable fix. If none fits, autonomous learning starts, with the language model handling analysis, candidate picks, data planning, and strategy. The robot learns from execution and watching, trains in quasi-real time, and stores validated results in the local store for reuse. Through this loop, the robot turns execution and observation lessons into reusable skill, cutting dependence on repeated model help.
arxiv-2604-22299: Barvinsky, Kalugin and Wachowski study off-diagonal asymptotic series for kernels of Laplace-type operators on curved backgrounds. Such expansions come from transforms of the DeWitt heat-kernel series, with basis kernels that are hypergeometric-type functions of the Synge world function. Basis kernels for a class of operator functions were previously found as N-fold Mellin-Barnes integrals. The authors study series representations of those integrals in non-resonant and resonant cases. They also suggest a physical reading of the emerging series, tied to ultraviolet and infrared properties.
arxiv-2604-22399: Chi and six colleagues build chip-based f-2f interferometry in tapered lithium niobate waveguides. Broadband generation offers a chip route to such work using coexisting second- and third-order nonlinear effects. Unlike uniform waveguides, their tapered waveguide varies width in a dual phase-matching window, supporting wave emission and harmonic generation. That design yields broad overlap and robust carrier-envelope offset readout at far lower pulse energies. A compact module works under temperature swings and with 500 MHz lasers, locking that frequency at 48 dB.
arxiv-2604-22499: Colot and four colleagues present continuous estimation of high-dimensional finger kinematics from forearm electromyography. Their framework combines an 8-channel EMG armband, a webcam and synchronisation, collecting the EMG-FK dataset, 10 hours of EMG and 15 joint angles from 20 participants. They also introduce the Temporal Riemannian Regressor, a lightweight GRU model using multi-band Riemannian covariance features to decode finger motion. Across that dataset and emg2pose, it beats leading methods in intra- and cross-subject evaluation, with average errors of about 10 degrees intra-subject and about 17 degrees cross-subject.
arxiv-2604-22599: Hess and Chopra study rare-earth nuclei's 0+ spectrum through the pseudo-SU(3) shell model. The 0+ spectrum of heavy nuclei has drawn attention in recent decades. Applied to Sm, Gd, Dy, Er, Yb, and Hf isotopes, the model explains the 0+ spectrum and state accumulation at certain energies, accounting for Pauli exclusion. A simple model Hamiltonian uses only the valence shell to highlight cross features. The microscopic Hilbert space proves essential for 0+ state accumulation, and gamma-band B(E2) transitions dominate beta-band ones trivially, unlike in some collective models.
arxiv-2604-22699: Anderson, Bakshi, and Hopkins tackle entrywise low-rank approximation: finding the closest low-rank matrix under an entrywise norm. Singular value decomposition solves this only for the squared case. For every even exponent above two and any fixed rank, they give the first approximation scheme, built on the Sherali-Adams hierarchy rather than sketching or column choice. The same strategy yields new additive approximations for matrix norms linked to small-set expansion and quantum information.
arxiv-2604-22799: Eich and six colleagues describe a user-centered route to greener shared computing at the VISPA physics cluster. The cluster sits in a 1970s building, where hardware upgrades alone would save little energy. Job-level energy tracking, weekly reports, carbon footprints, and scheduling into periods of high renewable power let researchers see and trim their own impact voluntarily. Memory records from earlier runs curb oversized requests, and simulations test how far awareness and choice can cut emissions over time.
arxiv-2604-23099: Huang and three colleagues offer ProEval, a cheap way to judge generative AI models by predicting scores and hunting failures early. Pretrained Gaussian Processes stand in for the score function, mapping inputs to error or safety risk, while Bayesian quadrature estimates performance and superlevel sampling seeks failures. Theory shows the estimator unbiased and bounded, and tests on reasoning, safety, and classification benchmarks back the design. ProEval needs 8 to 65 times fewer samples for estimates within 1 percent of truth, surfacing more varied failures under a tight budget.
arxiv-2604-23199: De Paoli and Pirozzoli test how fluid models and boundary settings change mixing predictions for buried carbon dioxide storage. High-detail runs cover linear, nonlinear, and non-monotonic density laws in two and three dimensions, with fixed and free interfaces. Across all cases, mean scalar dissipation tracks mixing, giving one frame for convective-diffusive links. Free interfaces boost early mixing by warping, while plain models such as monotonic laws or two-dimensional flow can skew mixing rates by up to about one hundred percent.
arxiv-2604-23599: Noorizadegan introduces PU-GKAN, a Gaussian Kolmogorov-Arnold network whose edge activations are normalised by their local sum, forming a partition of unity. The design reproduces constants exactly at each edge and admits a clear kernel interpretation, with a practical rule for choosing the scale parameter. Experiments show it is less sensitive to that scale, more accurate on most smooth and rough targets, and more stable in training.
arxiv-2604-23699: Choi builds a semantic-structural atlas of transportation research from over 120,000 papers across 34 journals spanning 1967 to 2025. Topic communities from semantic similarity agree only weakly with coauthor communities, and a combined partition locates where collaboration and topic structure decouple. His core finding defines phantom collaborators, semantically close authors far apart in the coauthor graph, who become real coauthors at many times the baseline rate.
arxiv-2604-23899: Oliveira compares light models for breast lesion segmentation against a U-Net baseline on the INbreast dataset. MobileNetV2 with squeeze-and-excitation achieves the best Dice score while using about three-quarters fewer weights than U-Net. Cross-dataset tests show lower scores from domain shift but preserved recall. The results support light models as a practical balance of quality and speed for usable screening systems.
arxiv-2604-24099: Cho and Kim study single-copy stabilizer learning, identifying a stabilizer group from one copy of a quantum state at a time. On average, logarithmic-depth local Clifford circuits suffice to learn almost all groups with logarithmically many non-stabilizer qubits, replacing the linear-depth measurements of earlier methods, with simulations up to 100 qubits in support. In the worst case, however, any adaptive single-copy scheme needs samples exponential in that count. Together with two-copy results, the findings point to a quantum learning advantage for large non-stabilizer counts.
arxiv-2604-24499: Carrino and Hohenegger ask how accurately the dynamics of a multi-degree system can be rebuilt from sampled measurements, using Fisher information as the size of an infinitesimal step along the system's path. They compute the bias of that estimate for large samples and show that grouping degrees of freedom into clusters reduces the bias. A simple compartmental model illustrates how clustering lets the same data describe the system more accurately.
arxiv-2604-24599: Liu and four colleagues expose a practical weakness in object-detection transformers: patch triggers tuned at fixed spots fail when real triggers vary in size, viewpoint and location. They observe a trigger radiating effect, where a patch trigger also activates the backdoor at neighboring spots, strengthened by placing triggers at several locations. Their DETOUR attack rescales semantic triggers, such as a mug pattern seen from many viewpoints, so the backdoor fires across the whole image.
arxiv-2604-25299: Sun and three colleagues propose a recursive mixture-of-experts framework for text-to-image diffusion models. Diffusion models succeed at synthesis, yet text following remains constrained. Their approach adds a recursive part to joint attention layers that refines visual tokens while sharing weights via sparse module choice. A gating network selects expert modules at each step, guided by current visual tokens. ImageNet, GenEval and DPG tests show gains in image generation.
arxiv-2604-25399: Gao and eight colleagues put forth CoRE, a code reasoning benchmark past output prediction. Past benchmarks grade only final output under one build, leaving gaps: steadiness across equal builds, and mid-run reasoning. CoRE grades reasoning through implementation invariance and process transparency. Tests on eight LLMs show a robustness gap, with scores swinging across equal builds, and shallow execution, with right outputs but no grasp of mid-run states. Output-only grading is too thin to judge code reasoning. CoRE is pitched as a needed benchmark for faithful reasoning.
arxiv-2604-25799: Rahman and four colleagues build an ultra-low-power FPGA system that extracts cardiac features on-device from seismocardiography signals. Both spaceflight and ground monitoring demand real-time features on tiny battery-powered devices. Their design pairs training that accounts for quantization with a systolic-array accelerator for integer-only inference on a Lattice chip. It reaches 98 percent validation accuracy, with each inference under a tenth of a second. The work shows autonomous cardiac monitoring is feasible on very constrained hardware.
arxiv-2604-25999: Sinha and three colleagues study topological defects in non-unitary conformal field theories, built here with lattice models. They build impurity models and defect operators for the lattice system from restricted solid-on-solid models. Numerical work covers the energy spectrum, defect values, and thermal features, against theory. Flows of the renormalization group between fixed points are checked numerically.
arxiv-2604-26099: Ram and three colleagues present a chapter laying the math and physics groundwork for electromagnetic wave travel and scattering in dielectric media on quantum machines. Standard models of Maxwell's laws face limits from present-day hardware. Quantum machines are widely touted as far outpacing older hardware, raising the question whether that power can serve classical physics problems. The chapter gives the basic concepts needed to judge that question, framing quantum models of classical wave events as an open puzzle rather than a settled power.
arxiv-2604-26199: Hu and Liu studied silting-induced t-structures and co-t-structures on triangulated categories. They asked when those structures stay intact after restriction to a precompletion or a completion. They proved that contravariant finiteness of the silting subcategory is exactly the test that decides it, which yields a purely categorical check for right coherent rings. They also carried Koenig and Yang's links among silting objects, bounded structures, and simple-minded collections into metric categories, keeping the mutation rules and natural orders.
arxiv-2604-26499: Jana and Rani proved central limit theorems for linear eigenvalue statistics of matrix models whose entries have exploding moments, moments growing with matrix size. They covered elliptic, centrosymmetric, circulant, and inter-correlated block models. The proofs run through an asymptotic Wick formula. The work extends the classical central-limit picture to models where entry moments blow up with dimension.
arxiv-2604-27099: Davoudiasl, Houtz and Ipek propose Mesogenesis where the universe's baryon asymmetry comes only from Standard Model CP violation in B meson decays. Data on B meson decays into baryons plus missing energy constrain such models. The dark decay channel can dominate only in the early universe, when an ultralight scalar linking the dark sector and leptons lets thermal muons lower a dark fermion's mass. The channel shuts off as muon density falls, keeping it compatible with flavor data and LHC bounds, which future runs may test.
arxiv-2604-27399: Edgeman and eleven colleagues investigate a puzzle in the MIGDAL experiment, where an optical time projection chamber shows tracks brighter and wider than charge simulations predict. They test whether scintillation light made inside a GEM hole during an avalanche travels through the substrate and escapes through neighbouring holes. Measurements on glass, ceramic, and FR4 substrates confirm the broadening and find it strongest in glass. Applying the glass effect to tracks raises intensity by up to about 26 percent and width by about 31 percent, which may explain the MIGDAL excess.
arxiv-2604-27599: Bito, Ren, and He propose InvariRank, a listwise reranking tool for language-model recommendation that scores candidates in any presentation order. Listwise rerankers often let candidate order sway item scores and final rankings, so rankings can reflect prompt layout rather than user taste. InvariRank blocks cross-candidate attention with a fixed mask and cancels order effects through shared positional framing under rotary embeddings. It scores all candidates in one forward pass, without multi-order training, and tests show strong ranking quality with stable rankings across orders.
arxiv-2604-27699: Zhang and six colleagues present ValuePlanner, a layered design for active robot agents splitting value planning from actions. A language-model module reasons through value trade-offs to generate symbolic subgoals, which a PDDL planner turns into action plans, refined by closed-loop feedback. The team also proposes a value-centered test suite tracking value gain, taste match, and varied behavior. In the TongSim household world, ValuePlanner juggles clashing values into clear, long-horizon behavior missing from order-following and needs-driven rivals.
arxiv-2604-27999: A mixture-model study by ten Eikelder and Brunk asks what closure rules stay meaningful when identical phases of a mixture are merged. Under a small set of structural axioms, consistency under merging fixes the free-energy form to ideal mixing plus a symmetric mean-field term and a quadratic gradient penalty. The same demand forces the mobility matrix into a pairwise-exchange form, and numerical tests confirm the predicted reduction behaviour.
arxiv-2605-00099:
Jonas Jäger and 5 co-authors introduce quantum Gaussian processes, a Bayesian way to learn from quantum systems. Instead of learning a single best guess, the method keeps a prior belief about an unknown quantum transformation and updates it with data. The prior is built from the system's structure and symmetries.

The authors show that, under the right conditions, quantum processes that evolve unit by unit define Gaussian processes. That link allows regression, classification, and guided search directly on quantum data. For one family of simple fermionic systems, they prove the method stays both valid and scalable. Tests include long-range prediction, learning phase diagrams of many-body systems, and a quantum sensing task done with few samples.
arxiv-2605-00199:
Jugal Gajjar and Kamalasankari Subramaniakuppusamy tackle a trust problem in table question answering: readers cannot see which cells a model used. Their method, RSAT, trains small language models to reason step by step while citing the exact table cells behind each step.

Training runs in two phases. First the models learn a strict output format from checked reasoning traces. Then a reward-based phase scores them on faithfulness, sound citations, and brevity. Across six small models from two families, RSAT raised faithfulness sharply over format training alone, with near-perfect citation accuracy. Adding citations after the fact failed, which shows the checking must be built into the reasoning itself.
arxiv-2605-00299:
J. Haddad and D. Ryabogin work on a rigidity question in convex geometry. They consider a symmetric convex body of revolution in four dimensions that contains the unit ball. Through every plane tangent to that ball, the body is sliced, and every such slice is assumed to have the same area.

The authors prove that, under that condition, the body must itself be a Euclidean ball, at least when a certain number built from the shared area satisfies arithmetic conditions. Those conditions can be read off from the number's continued fraction expansion. They also show that the set of areas passing the test is reasonably large, in the sense of positive Hausdorff dimension. The result pins down how strongly constant section area constrains a body's shape.
arxiv-2605-00499:
Zhiying Deng and 5 co-authors improve next-basket recommendation, predicting the set of items a shopper will buy next from their history of baskets. Two motives drive a basket: habitual repurchase of familiar items, and exploration of new ones. Most models tangle the two in a single representation, letting habits drown out discovery, and they ignore the continuous time gaps and rhythms between purchases.

Their model, TIDE, separates the motives into two experts, one for habits and one guided to explore, with a gate that balances them per item. A time encoding enhanced with Hawkes-style decay and Fourier features captures each item's own periodicity. On four real-world datasets, TIDE consistently beat leading next-basket methods. The design lesson is that recommendation improves when rival motives get separate machinery and time is treated as continuous.
arxiv-2605-00899:
James Flora, Kowshik Thopalli, Akshay R. Kulkarni, Weng-Keen Wong, and Shusen Liu present LatentDiff, a scalable way to compare image datasets by meaning rather than by captions. The framework works directly in the latent space of pretrained vision encoders. It combines divergence testing based on sparse autoencoders with density ratio estimation to surface interpretable semantic differences at a fraction of the cost of caption-based methods.

The team also introduces Noisy-Diff, a benchmark for realistic sparse shifts where only a tiny fraction of images differ, a setting where existing methods struggle. Experiments show LatentDiff keeps superior accuracy and stays robust even when the differing share falls from a few percent to below one percent.
arxiv-2605-00999:
Thiago C. A. de Carvalho and three co-authors study layered control of a one-dimensional Stefan problem, which models a moving phase boundary such as melting ice. Their setting combines a Stackelberg strategy, where a leader acts first, with a Nash equilibrium among multiple followers. That creates a multi-objective free-edge problem with localized distributed controls.

The interplay between hierarchy and the moving interface produces a nonlinear optimality system. The original problem reduces to null controllability of that system. Under suitable geometric conditions on control regions, the authors prove a local null control result using an observability bound from Carleman estimates adapted to a moving edge. They present the work as the first Stefan treatment in this framework.
arxiv-2605-01099:
Daniel J. Heimsoth, A. Baha Balantekin, and Pooja Siwach simulate a self-interacting three-flavor neutrino system inside a core-collapse supernova using a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm on a qutrit computer. Neutrino flavor change in that environment is demanding to compute. Based on Dirac-Frenkel evolution equations, their quantum-assisted simulator uses qutrit Hadamard tests to find expectation values needed for the time-step operator, while the stepping itself is carried out classically.

The hybrid method matches exact numerical integration out to the times tested, with a small time step relative to the vacuum oscillation scale. The authors discuss lessons for simulating such systems this way, along with advantages the approach offers over quantum Trotterization. That method is a common alternative for time stepping on quantum hardware.
arxiv-2605-01199:
Zheng-An Chen, Pengxiao Lin, Zhi-Qin John Xu, and Tao Luo trace how attention learns inside a Transformer, the model type behind modern language tools. Training dynamics are still poorly mapped, so the team studies a one-layer model fed with step-by-step data that follows simple transition rules.

They find a repeating cycle of focus and dilution. First the word vectors shrink to a rank-one form while attention stays still. Attention then grows and locks onto frequent tokens. That shift stirs the word vectors, spreads the focus out, and small gaps among rare tokens open new directions, starting the cycle again. Tests on synthetic data and on two text sets, WikiText and TinyStories, match the stages the theory predicts.
arxiv-2605-01399:
Sangkwon Park, Donghun Kang, Jisoo Mok, and Sungroh Yoon improve retrieval-augmented generation, where a language model answers with help from fetched texts. Dropping raw fetched text into the prompt often leaves the model to guess how each passage bears on the question.

Their fix adds verbal annotations: short analytic notes that spell out the logical link between the query and each passage. A test study shows such notes can lift answer accuracy a lot. The full system, Verbal-R3, pairs a generator that loops between fetching and reasoning with a verbal reranker that scores passages and writes the notes to guide the next step. A relevance-guided rule spends extra test-time compute where it helps most. On hard question-answering benchmarks, Verbal-R3 sets new best scores.
arxiv-2605-01699:
Anamika Paul Rupa and Anietie Andy hunt the fingerprints that unlearning leaves inside a language model. Deleting memorized content by behavior alone can leave internal traces that a probing adversary can still read. The authors first map where the trace lives. A leave-one-out probe tests whether a memorization signal carries across unseen sequences.

The signal proves real across model sizes, and it is causally separate from recall: erase its direction and the probe's edge collapses while the model's actual memory of text barely moves. Their erasure method aligns activations along the probe's live readout direction at each depth, one rank-one fix per layer. The cross-sequence probe then falls below chance at every scale tested. It survives six adversarial probe variants and even beats an attacker who retrains a fresh probe. Capability scores on standard tasks stay essentially unmoved throughout.
arxiv-2605-02099:
Enes Makalic and Daniel Schmidt introduce entropic strict minimum message length, a risk-sensitive version of a classic coding rule for model choice. Strict minimum message length picks the model with the shortest expected two-part code. The new criterion replaces that average with an exponential certainty equivalent, giving a family of rules set by one risk parameter.

At the risk-neutral limit, the original rule returns. At the extreme limit, the rule becomes a worst-case minimax code. Applied to regret against an oracle code, the same idea recovers normalised maximum likelihood. The authors also give a variational form with a divergence penalty, a PAC-Bayes style reading, and asymptotics for how the risk parameter and sample size interact.
arxiv-2605-02199:
Nishant Bhargava and Rodrigo Sobral Barrento introduce MEMAUDIT, a protocol for judging how well an agent writes long-term memory under a storage budget. Agents must compress a stream of past interactions before future questions are known. Past tests measured only final answer accuracy, which mixes writing with retrieval, prompting, and reader skill.

A MEMAUDIT package fixes the experience stream, candidate memory forms, storage costs, evidence units, future needs, and a budget. Memory choice then becomes a finite optimisation problem with a certified best score. The authors instantiate it with a coverage objective under storage and one-form-per-experience rules, solving packages exactly by branch-and-bound with mixed-integer certification. Tests include stress cases and human-audited slices.
arxiv-2605-02599:
Roelof Bruggeman and three co-authors give a cohomological account of cusp forms on rank-one symmetric spaces. Cusp forms are special waves on such a space that fade at its ends, and they carry deep number-theoretic information. The setting covers any rank-one space of noncompact type, with a discrete group of symmetries that is finite in volume but not compact.

The authors identify certain group submodules inside a principal series representation, and matching subspaces of parabolic cohomology in the top relevant degree. Explicit isomorphisms link the cusp forms of a given spectral parameter to those cohomology classes. One direction is an integral transform, and its inverse uses a reproducing property of that transform. The account is uniform across all such spaces and does not rely on sorting them by type.
arxiv-2605-02899:
Shojibur Rahman and four co-authors measure how the mental load of shopping online shifts with product prices, using eye tracking. Site design shapes buying choices and satisfaction, and a cluttered page imposes cognitive load that spoils the experience. Price, the authors argue, is a driver of that perceived complexity, not just a number on the page.

Forty-eight participants browsed well-known e-commerce sites while their eye movements were calibrated and recorded. Load was read from fixation counts, saccades, fixation duration, and task time. The same product at different price ranges drew different complexity responses, the study reports, and customer perception tracked visual complexity closely during purchase decisions. The authors offer the findings to developers and business analysts who want calmer, clearer shopping pages.
arxiv-2605-02999:
S. Weng and forty-one co-authors catalogue gas flowing into galaxies, using spectra from a major survey's second data release. How galaxies gain their gas is a core open question in the baryon cycle, yet direct evidence is scarce. The team searches for absorption by neutral sodium seen against each galaxy's own light, a down-the-barrel view that catches gas on the near side, across millions of galaxies at modest redshift.

Bayesian evidence tests separate true interstellar absorption from the galaxy's systemic signal. Tens of thousands of galaxies show moderate to strong evidence for extra absorption. About half the flow components move inward, and a strong case emerges for a large population of slow inflows in edge-on galaxies, matching simulated radial infall. In early-type galaxies, inflow speed tracks the spread of stellar speeds more than stellar mass.
arxiv-2605-03099:
David C. Flynn assembles a machine-readable corpus of Milky Way globular cluster parameters drawn from four published surveys. Globular clusters are dense star swarms whose basic data were scattered across catalogs with different formats and coverage.

The corpus covers 174 clusters with over seventeen thousand data points in open formats, each with clear types and provenance notes. It merges Harris photometry, Gaia proper motions, N-body masses and orbits, and APOGEE chemistry where available. Built for retrieval-augmented language model use, it also serves orbit modeling, classification, chemical tagging, and cross-survey checks by researchers.
arxiv-2605-03199:
Shafi Ullah Khan, Madan Baduwal, Vini Chaudhary, and Debashri Roy propose PERFECT, a personalized federated system for detecting naval radar in the shared CBRS band. Sensors must spot faint radar amid heavy phone network traffic, while central training raises privacy worries and sensor data differ by location.

PERFECT trains locally on each sensor and personalizes models where sites see distinct radar types, so raw data never leaves the sensor. In simulations it reached the required ninety-nine percent radar recall, matching central training while improving privacy, efficiency, and scale. The design fits the varied, spread-out sensing network that guards the band.
arxiv-2605-03299:
Minh Chu Xuan, Tien-Phat Nguyen, Linh Ngo Van, Dinh Viet Sang, Nguyen Thi Ngoc Diep, and Trung Le present LLM-XTM, a framework that uses large language models to sharpen cross-lingual topic models. Finding shared themes across languages usually leans on scarce bilingual resources and often yields weak, poorly aligned topics.

Cheaper document-level language model fixes can hallucinate and may need hidden token scores. LLM-XTM instead adds guided refinement with self-consistency uncertainty checks, working with black-box models in a stable, scalable way. On multilingual corpora it improved topic coherence and cross-language alignment while cutting reliance on dictionaries and costly model calls.
arxiv-2605-03499:
Dario Filatrella, Ragnar Thobaben, and Mikael Skoglund bound the generalization error of hierarchical federated learning using Wasserstein distance. In hierarchical setups, data are sampled through a tree of clients and servers, creating dependencies that flat analyses ignore.

Their framework models that sampling tree directly and measures how swapping one node changes the algorithm's output. The resulting bounds recover and strictly extend leading mutual information bounds for bounded losses. They also combine with differential privacy assumptions to yield privacy-based bounds. On a Gaussian location model, the bound recovers the true asymptotic error rate.
arxiv-2605-03599:
Guodong Yu and twelve co-authors propose a fusion device that merges the two leading magnetic confinement designs, the tokamak and the stellarator. Tokamaks rely on simple ring-shaped coils plus plasma current, while stellarators use shaped external fields for steady operation. Their hybrid keeps a tokamak-like coil set and adds 288 dipole-field coils.

Only six independent coil shapes are needed, thanks to symmetry. By programming the coil currents, the same hardware can produce more than 1.66 million optimized stellarator configurations, spanning several symmetry types, plus tokamak-like three-dimensional perturbations. Sample configurations show nested magnetic surfaces, low transport losses, and good confinement of energetic particles, enabling fast design searches without rebuilding hardware.
arxiv-2605-04099:
Hamzeh Alavirad presents a time-resolved digital quantum simulation of particle creation during a cosmological transition from a de Sitter phase to a radiation phase. Rather than compiling only the final Bogoliubov transformation into a one-shot circuit, it discretizes the evolution in conformal time and runs it as a sequence of short-time circuit blocks. That gives access to how particle occupation builds up during the transition, not just the late-time count.

A four-qubit encoding represents a momentum pair in the single-excitation regime. Matrix-Trotter evolution, noiseless statevector simulation, finite-shot runs, and a shallow run on IBM hardware are compared. Simulator results matched the analytic sudden-transition benchmark. The hardware run executed the shallow block but carried a residual error around one percent. Full reconstruction of the particle spectrum remains beyond current noisy devices.
arxiv-2605-04199:
Federico Battiston and six co-authors review what happens when dynamics unfold on multiplex networks, where the same nodes connect through several kinds of links at once. Social, biological, and ecological systems often work this way, with each layer carrying a different type of interaction.

The review covers processes such as spreading, synchronisation, diffusion, and games, plus cases where two processes evolve together or a process reshapes the network itself. Throughout, the authors stress behaviour that only appears because of the layered structure, and that vanishes if the layers are merged or studied one by one. They close by naming open challenges.
arxiv-2605-04299:
Maryam Sadat Hosseini Azad and Shahriar Baradaran Shokouhi work on making self-driving car perception easier to explain and trust. A driving system must predict several behaviours at once and give reasons, yet the deep models behind it are hard to see into.

They study how the confidence threshold for accepting a prediction changes results across tasks, showing that one fixed threshold is a poor fit for multi-task systems. Their adaptive choice improves scores across tasks. They also introduce a new data set of just under a thousand human-annotated images to support cross-cultural testing of explainable driving systems.
arxiv-2605-04399:
Nathaniel Sagman and Thomas-René Thalmaier prove a result about stable minimal surfaces, shapes that locally minimise area and do not lower it further under small deformations. The question is when such a surface must secretly be holomorphic, that is, governed by complex-analytic structure.

For surfaces of the simplest topology, including some with infinite total curvature, they prove a sharp test. Stability holds exactly when the surface lies in an even-dimensional flat subspace. It must also be holomorphic for a suitable structure there. Their method builds explicit deformations, so unstable surfaces come with concrete ways to destabilise them and measured radii for doing so.
arxiv-2605-04499:
Yasod Ginige and three co-authors present a framework to help automated penetration testing, the practice of probing computer systems for weaknesses before attackers do. A shortage of skilled security professionals drives interest in automation, but language-model agents often plan poorly, reason weakly about the domain, and pick the wrong tools.

Their system pairs a specialised reasoning model with a classifier. The model is fine-tuned with reinforcement learning on a new data set of explained pentesting strategies. The classifier turns a strategy into concrete steps. On their test split, the reasoning model formed strategies successfully in most cases, improving on general-purpose agent frameworks.
arxiv-2605-04599:
Antoine Baron and five co-authors show that electrochemically grown polymer patterns can act as physical fingerprints. Living things balance control and randomness to produce textures, like those on leaves or skin, that identify both a species and an individual, and the authors mimic that balance with electrochemistry.

Growing a conducting polymer on a surface produces wildly varied coatings of spots, rosettes, or marbled patterns. Despite their randomness, the patterns reliably reflect the growth conditions, especially the chemical makeup of the solution used. A statistical study shows the patterns could tag a solution's identity within a class, pointing toward uses in physical identification and encryption.
